materials.passage:
A Greener Street: Weighing the Trade-offs

[A] Last month, the Riverside Community Group met to discuss a plan for Green Street. The plan has three parts: more trees, new bike lanes, and a small garden. The group wants a cleaner and quieter street. However, some people are worried about the cost and the changes.

[B] “If we plant more trees, the air will be cleaner,” said Mrs. Chen, the group leader. “Trees also make the street cooler in summer. But we must think about the cost. Each tree costs about 200 yuan, and we need 30 trees. Therefore, we need to raise 6,000 yuan.” Mr. Li, a shop owner, said, “If you take away parking spaces for bike lanes, some customers will go to other streets. Because my shop needs parking, I am worried.”

[C] The group also talked about the small garden. “If we build the garden, children will have a safe place to play,” said Mrs. Chen. “But we should ask the children what they want. We could also ask a gardener for advice.” Mr. Li suggested, “Why don’t we keep some parking and add trees only? Then we can have cleaner air and no lost parking.” Another member said, “We must not forget the noise. If we plant trees near the road, the noise will be less.”

[D] In the end, the group agreed on a new plan. They will plant 20 trees and build a small garden, but they will not take away parking spaces. They will ask the children for ideas about the garden. Mrs. Chen said, “We should listen to everyone. If we work together, we will find a good answer.” The group will meet again next month to check the cost.

grammar.title: 第一条件句、because/therefore、情态动词建议
grammar.explanation: 本课学习三个语法点。第一，第一条件句表示“如果……就会……”：If + 一般现在时，主句用 will + 动词原形。例如：If we plant more trees, the air will be cleaner. 第二，because 表示原因，therefore 表示结果。because 引导原因从句，therefore 是副词，前面常用逗号。例如：Because my shop needs parking, I am worried. / We need 30 trees. Therefore, we need to raise 6,000 yuan. 第三，情态动词 should, could, must 用于提建议。should 表示“应该”，could 表示“可以（较委婉）”，must 表示“必须”。例如：We should ask the children what they want. / We could also ask a gardener for advice. / We must not forget the noise. 注意：第一条件句中，if 从句不用 will，主句才用 will。

materials.instructions: 这是一份为B1水平成人学习者设计的英语听力与语法练习，主题为“环境与原因结果”。场景为模拟的社区花园会议，所有内容均为原创教学材料，并非官方雅思考试。请先听/读对话，然后完成8道听力理解题（单选、填空、匹配、判断正误/未提及）。之后学习“第一条件句；because / therefore；情态动词建议”的语法规则，并完成8道语法题。最后进行口语和写作迁移练习。所有题目和选项均为英文，解释为中文。
materials.transcript:
Mia: Thanks for coming, everyone. This is the first meeting of the Green Street Garden Group. We have a small piece of land behind the library. We can use it, but we must decide how.
Ben: I think we should grow vegetables. If we grow vegetables, we can share them with families who need food.
Mia: That's a good idea. But we need water. The tap is far away. If we don't have enough water, the plants will die.
Ben: True. Therefore, we should collect rain water. We can put a big barrel under the roof.
Mia: Good. But a barrel costs money. We have only fifty dollars.
Ben: Hmm. If we buy a barrel, we can't buy seeds. Maybe we can ask the school for help.
Mia: Yes. Let's ask the school. Also, we need volunteers. If we have more volunteers, we can work faster.
Ben: I can ask my neighbors. But some people don't like gardens. They say gardens make noise.
Mia: That's a problem. Therefore, we should talk to them first. We can invite them to join us.
Ben: OK. And we should not use chemicals. If we use chemicals, the soil will get bad.
Mia: Right. So we will use natural compost. It is cheap and good for the soil.
Ben: What about the tools? We need shovels and gloves.
Mia: We can borrow tools from the community center. They have many.
Ben: Great. So, if we get the barrel and the tools, we can start next month.
Mia: Yes. Let's meet again next week. Thank you, everyone.

materials.passage:
A.  
Mia is 42 years old. She works in a small shop. Last year, she wanted to learn English. She went to the community learning centre near her home. The centre has evening classes for adults. Mia joined a class in September. She has studied there for eight months. She has already finished two books. She has not taken a test yet.

B.  
The centre has changed a lot since 2020. In the past, only young people came to the centre. Now, many older adults come too. The centre has opened a new computer room. It has also started free weekend classes. Mia's teacher, Mr. Chen, has worked at the centre since 2015. He says, "Adult learners are very busy. They have families and jobs. But they are also very serious."

C.  
Mia has made new friends in her class. Her friend, Tom, is 55. He has worked in a factory for thirty years. He has just started learning English. He has not missed a class yet. Mia and Tom have already planned to take a test next year. They have not decided which test yet. Mia says, "I have never felt too old to learn."

grammar.explanation: 现在完成时表示过去发生的动作对现在造成的影响或结果，或从过去开始持续到现在的动作/状态。结构：have/has + 过去分词。already 用于肯定句，表示“已经”；yet 用于否定句和疑问句，表示“还（没）”或“已经”；since 后接时间点，表示“自从”；for 后接时间段，表示“持续了多久”。一般过去时只表示过去发生的动作，与现在无关。例如：She has studied there for eight months.（现在完成时，强调持续到现在） vs. She studied there last year.（一般过去时，只说明过去）。

materials.transcript:
Maya: Hi Tom. You look happy today.
Tom: Yes! I started a new evening class at the community centre. It's a computer class.
Maya: Really? When did you start?
Tom: I started last Monday. I have already finished two lessons.
Maya: Wow, that's fast. Have you done any homework yet?
Tom: No, I haven't done any homework yet. The teacher gives us homework on Friday.
Maya: How long is the course?
Tom: It's for ten weeks. I have been in the class since last Monday.
Maya: Is it expensive?
Tom: No, it's free for adults over eighteen. The centre has offered free classes for three years.
Maya: That's great. I have wanted to learn computers for a long time.
Tom: You should join! The next class is on Wednesday. Have you ever used a computer before?
Maya: Yes, I have used one at work, but only for email. I haven't used other programs yet.
Tom: That's fine. The teacher is very patient. She has taught here since 2019.
Maya: Has she given you a book?
Tom: Yes, she has already given us a small book. It's easy to read.
Maya: Good. I will call the centre tomorrow. I have not called them yet.
Tom: Do it soon. The class is small. Only twelve people have joined so far.
Maya: OK. Thanks, Tom. See you on Wednesday!
Tom: See you!

materials.instructions: 这是一份为B1水平成人学习者设计的原创英语阅读材料（第17周），主题为“教育与已发生的变化”。所有场景与数据均为模拟教学材料，并非真实研究，也不代表任何官方考试或分数。请先阅读文章，完成8道阅读题；然后学习“现在完成时入门”的语法讲解，并完成8道语法题；最后完成口语与写作任务。阅读题和语法题的题干与选项均为英文，解释为中文。
materials.passage:
A. At the Westbridge Adult Learning Centre, four learners meet on Tuesday evenings. Their teacher, Ms. Chen, asked them to test a study method for three weeks. The method is simple: use flashcards for fifteen minutes every day. The group wants to know if the method works. They have collected their own data, and now they are discussing the evidence.

B. “I have used flashcards since the first week,” says Marco. “I already know fifty new words. Before, I forgot words quickly. Now I remember them.” Lena disagrees. “I have not finished my flashcard set yet. I started late, so my numbers are low. But I have studied with a partner for two weeks, and that helps me more.”

C. Ms. Chen shows a chart. “You have all improved since September. But please be careful. You have also changed other things. Marco, you have read a short news story every morning since week two. Lena, you have watched English videos for twenty minutes a day. So we cannot say flashcards alone made the difference.”

D. The group decides to run a cleaner test. For the next two weeks, they will use flashcards only, with no videos and no news stories. They have not started this new test yet. “We have learned one important thing already,” says Marco. “Good evidence needs patience.”

materials.instructions: 本材料为原创模拟练习，不是官方雅思试题，也不代表任何正式分数。请先听/读对话，注意现在完成时（have/has + 过去分词）与一般过去时的区别，以及 already / yet / since / for 的用法。完成 8 道听力/阅读题后，学习语法讲解并做 8 道语法题。所有题目选项均为英文，解释为中文。
materials.transcript:
Mia: Hi, Ben. You look happy. Have you finished your study project yet?
Ben: Yes, I have. I finished it on Monday. I have already sent it to our teacher.
Mia: Great. I haven't started my part yet. I'm a little worried.
Ben: Don't worry. I have used a new study method for two weeks. It really helps.
Mia: Really? What method?
Ben: I have studied in short blocks since the beginning of this month. Twenty minutes of work, then a five-minute break.
Mia: That sounds simple. Have you tried it for math?
Ben: Yes, I have. I did math for three blocks yesterday. I also made flashcards for new words.
Mia: I tried flashcards last year, but I stopped after one week. They didn't work for me.
Ben: Maybe you used too many cards. I have made only ten cards so far. I review them every evening.
Mia: That's a good idea. Have you told our teacher about this method?
Ben: No, I haven't told her yet. But I have written a short report. I finished it last night.
Mia: Can I read it? I have never read a student report about study methods.
Ben: Sure. I have just printed a copy. Here you are.
Mia: Thanks. I have already learned something new from this conversation.
Ben: Me too. I have not used my phone during study time for five days. That has helped a lot.

grammar.title: 现在完成时入门：already / yet / since / for 与一般过去时的区别
grammar.explanation: 现在完成时表示“到现在为止已经发生或未发生的事”，结构是 have/has + 过去分词。already 用于肯定句，表示“已经”；yet 用于否定句和疑问句，表示“还（没）”或“已经（吗）”；since 后接时间点（如 since Monday），for 后接时间段（如 for two weeks）。一般过去时只说明过去某个时间发生的事，常与明确过去时间连用（如 yesterday, last year, on Monday）。比较：I finished it on Monday.（过去具体时间） vs. I have finished it.（现在完成，强调结果）。注意：have/has 不随主语的人称变化而改变过去分词形式。

materials.passage:
A. Mei is a Chinese adult learner. She wants to choose a digital tool for her father. Her father is 68 years old. He lives in a small town. He wants to learn English for travel. He has a smartphone, but he does not like small buttons. He needs a simple tool.

B. Mei compares three apps. The first app is very popular. It has many lessons. But the lessons are long. Her father gets tired after 20 minutes. The second app is for children. It has bright colors and games. Her father feels strange using it. The third app is new. It has short lessons. Each lesson is 10 minutes. The app also has a big button for listening. Her father can press it easily.

C. Mei reads reviews. One review says, "The short lessons are good for old users." Another review says, "The app is free, but it has ads." Mei's father does not like ads. Mei finds a setting to remove ads. It costs 20 yuan each month. Her father agrees to pay. He says, "I want to learn to speak English for my trip." Mei helps him download the app. Now her father uses it every day. He listens to English for 10 minutes. Then he repeats the sentences. He is happy because the tool is easy to use.

materials.transcript:
Mia: Hi, Ben. You look busy. What are you doing?
Ben: I'm trying to choose a note-taking app for my dad. He's 65 and not good with technology.
Mia: OK. What does he need it for?
Ben: He wants to remember his medicines and doctor visits. He also needs to share lists with my mom.
Mia: So the app must be simple. Does he use a smartphone?
Ben: Yes, but he only uses it for calls and photos. He doesn't like small buttons.
Mia: Then a simple app with big text is better. Have you looked at 'EasyNote'?
Ben: Yes, I downloaded it yesterday. But it has too many ads. My dad gets confused by ads.
Mia: What about 'SimpleList'? It's designed for older users. It has no ads and the text is large.
Ben: That sounds good. Is it free?
Mia: The basic version is free. You pay for extra features, but your dad doesn't need them.
Ben: Can he share lists with my mom?
Mia: Yes, sharing is included in the free version. But you need to set it up for him first.
Ben: OK. I'll install it on his phone tonight. Thanks, Mia.
Mia: You're welcome. Remember to write a short guide for him.
Ben: Good idea. I'll do that.

materials.passage:
A. At a small company called Bright Tools, the support team met on Monday. The manager, Ms. Chen, wanted to discuss automation. 'We need to decide how to use new software to help our customers,' she said. 'Some tasks are slow, and we want to answer questions faster.' The team had eight people. They all listened carefully.

B. Tom, a senior agent, raised his hand. 'I think we should use a chatbot to answer simple questions,' he said. 'Customers can get help at night. The chatbot is designed to give quick answers. But we must keep the human team for difficult problems.' Other people nodded. 'We need to train the chatbot to understand common questions,' Ms. Chen said. 'That takes time.'

C. Lily disagreed. 'I enjoy talking to customers,' she said. 'A chatbot cannot show empathy. People feel happy when they speak to a real person. We should not replace people with machines.' She looked worried. 'Our job is to support people, not to save money.'

D. Ms. Chen listened. 'You are right, Lily,' she said. 'We will not replace anyone. The chatbot will only handle simple questions. The team will focus on complex issues. We plan to start next month. Tom will lead the training.' The team felt relieved. They agreed to try the new system together.

Tom: Good idea. I'll prepare a report to show the benefits and risks.

materials.passage: Last week, a group of neighbours met in the community hall. They were planning a lantern festival for the town. Mrs Chen was leading the meeting. While she was writing notes on the board, Mr Li arrived with a box of old lanterns. "These are from my grandfather," he said. "He was a lantern maker." The group needed a theme. A young woman named Anna suggested "Stories of Our Town." Everyone liked the idea. They decided to ask people to make lanterns about local people. One lantern would show the baker who opens his shop at 5 a.m. Another would show the nurse who works at the small clinic. Mrs Chen said, "We need a place for the event." Mr Li said the park was free on Saturday. While they were talking, the town librarian came in. She offered to display old photos of the town. The group was happy. They planned to meet again on Thursday. At the end, Mrs Chen said, "Remember, the lanterns which we make must be safe." Everyone agreed. The festival will be on the last Saturday of the month.

materials.transcript:
Mia: Hi, Ben. Are you free on Saturday? We are organising a lantern festival in the community hall.
Ben: A lantern festival? That sounds fun. What do you need help with?
Mia: Well, I was making lanterns yesterday when my sister called. She said she could help too. While I was cutting paper, she was painting the lanterns.
Ben: Great. Who is the person in charge of the food?
Mia: That's Mr. Chen. He is the man who owns the noodle shop on Green Street. He was cooking soup when I asked him.
Ben: Nice. And which room are we using?
Mia: Room 2, the big room which has a stage. We were moving tables there when the caretaker told us to stop.
Ben: Why did he stop you?
Mia: He said the floor was wet. So we waited. While we were waiting, we talked about the programme.
Ben: What programme?
Mia: There is a story-telling corner for children, and a dance show that starts at seven. The dance group which practises here every week will perform.
Ben: I see. Was anyone taking photos last year?
Mia: Yes, a student who studies photography took them. This year, we want someone who can make a short video too.
Ben: I can do that. I was learning video editing last month.
Mia: Perfect! While you were learning, we were planning the posters. Can you come at five?
Ben: Sure. I'll bring my camera which has a good microphone.
Mia: Thanks, Ben. See you on Saturday!

materials.title: Two Stories About the Lantern Walk
materials.instructions: 阅读下面的短文，回答8个问题。短文和问题均为英文，解释为中文。这是模拟教学材料，不是官方雅思考试。请先通读全文，再做题。
materials.passage:
A
Every year in our town, people walk with lanterns on the first night of the moon festival. This year, I heard two different stories about why we do this. My neighbor, Mrs. Chen, is 78. She told me that long ago, farmers carried lanterns to their fields. They were looking for lost animals while the sun was going down. She said, "We were helping each other. The lanterns were small, but the night was dark." Her story is about kindness.

B
My friend Leo heard a different story from his grandfather. Leo's grandfather said that people carried lanterns to remember a famous teacher who lived in the mountains. The teacher taught children who had no school. While the teacher was walking home one evening, a storm came. People walked with lights to help him find the road. Leo said, "The teacher was very important to the village." This story is about respect for learning.

C
I asked my teacher, Mr. Wang, about the two stories. He smiled and said, "Both stories can be true. People remember different things. The lantern walk is a tradition that brings people together." He also said that the walk is not a race. "You walk slowly, and you talk with your neighbors. That is the important part." I like both stories. One is about helping, and one is about learning. Maybe that is why the walk is still popular today.

materials.transcript:
Mia: Hi, Ben. You look tired. Were you waiting for me?
Ben: Yes, I was. I was standing near the gate for twenty minutes. While I was waiting, I watched the lanterns.
Mia: Sorry! My grandmother was telling me a story about this festival. She says the lanterns are for a clever girl who saved our village.
Ben: That's interesting. My neighbor told me a different story. He says the lanterns are for a brave man who fought a dragon.
Mia: Really? Which story is true?
Ben: I don't know. Maybe both stories are old. People tell different stories about the same tradition.
Mia: My grandmother's story is about a girl who made a big fire on the hill. The fire helped travelers who were lost in the dark.
Ben: My neighbor's story is about a man who carried a lantern to the top of the hill. He wanted to warn people about a dragon that was coming.
Mia: Hmm. Both stories have a hill and a light. Maybe they are the same story, but people remember different parts.
Ben: That's possible. While we were talking, the sun went down. Look, people are lighting the lanterns now.
Mia: The lanterns are beautiful. Which one do you like best?
Ben: I like the red one that is shaped like a fish. What about you?
Mia: I like the small white one which is hanging near the tree. It looks like a star.
Ben: Do you think the stories matter?
Mia: Yes. The stories are the reason we come here every year. They connect us to the past.
Ben: You're right. Next year, I will ask my neighbor more questions. Maybe he knows more about the girl story too.
Mia: Good idea. And I will ask my grandmother about the dragon story. Maybe the two stories will become one.

materials.title: The Missing Skill: A Learner's Investigation
materials.instructions: 这是为B1水平成人学习者设计的原创模拟阅读材料（非官方雅思测试）。请先阅读文章，然后完成8道阅读理解题。题目类型包括单选、填空和判断正误/未提及。所有题目和选项均为英文，解释为中文。请仔细阅读文章，答案必须基于文章内容。
materials.passage:
A. Mei is a 28-year-old office worker in Shanghai. She has studied English for two years. She can read simple emails and write short messages. But she has a persistent problem: she cannot understand fast English speech. When she watches videos, people speak quickly and she misses many words. She feels frustrated.

B. Last week, Mei decided to investigate her skill gap. She recorded a short news video and listened to it five times. The first time, she understood only three words. The second time, she caught a few more. She wrote down every word she heard. Then she compared her notes with the video transcript. She found that she often missed small words like 'a', 'the', and 'to'. She also missed the endings of words, such as '-ed' and '-s'.

C. Mei made a plan. She will listen to one short video every day. She will pause after each sentence and repeat it. She will also practice listening to numbers and names, because these are common in news. Her teacher, Mr. Chen, says, 'Don't worry about every word. Focus on the main idea first.' Mei feels more confident now. She knows her gap and she has a clear plan.

grammar.title: 基础时态、问句、名词数量和常见从句综合复习
grammar.explanation: 本课重点复习一般现在时和一般过去时。一般现在时表示经常发生或习惯性动作，如 'She listens to a video every day.'；一般过去时表示过去发生的动作，如 'She listened to it five times.'。问句需要助动词，如 'Does she listen?' 或 'Did she listen?'。名词数量要注意可数与不可数，如 'a few words'（可数）和 'much information'（不可数）。常见从句如宾语从句 'She knows that she has a gap.' 和状语从句 'When she watches videos, she misses words.'。
grammar.example: She will listen to one short video every day.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She listen to music every day.
She listens to music every day.
She listening to music every day.
She is listen to music every day.
answers: She listens to music every day.
questions.explanation: 一般现在时，主语 She 是第三人称单数，动词要加 -s，因此 'She listens' 正确。
questions.evidence: She will listen to one short video every day.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct question.
questions.explanation: 一般过去时的问句用助动词 Did，后接动词原形 watch。因此 'Did she watch the video?' 正确。
questions.evidence: She recorded a short news video and listened to it five times.

questions.prompt: She ______ (study) English for two years.
questions.explanation: 现在完成时表示从过去持续到现在的动作，结构为 have/has + 过去分词。主语 She 用 has，study 的过去分词是 studied。
questions.evidence: She has studied English for two years.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence with a noun quantity.
questions.explanation: words 是可数名词复数，用 a few 修饰；information 不可数，不能用 many 修饰。因此 'a few words' 正确。
questions.evidence: She wrote down every word she heard.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence with a clause.
options: She knows that she has a gap.
She knows what she has a gap.
She knows that has she a gap.
She knows which she has a gap.
answers: She knows that she has a gap.
questions.explanation: 宾语从句用 that 引导，从句用陈述语序 'she has a gap'。因此第一句正确。
questions.evidence: She knows her gap and she has a clear plan.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence with a time clause.
options: When she watches videos, she misses words.
When she watch videos, she misses words.
When she watching videos, she misses words.
When she watched videos, she misses words.
answers: When she watches videos, she misses words.
questions.explanation: 时间状语从句用一般现在时表示经常性动作，主语 she 后动词加 -s，因此 'watches' 正确。
questions.evidence: When she watches videos, people speak quickly and she misses many words.

questions.prompt: ______ she listen to the video yesterday?
questions.explanation: 一般过去时的一般疑问句用助动词 Did 开头，后接主语和动词原形。
questions.evidence: She recorded a short news video and listened to it five times.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct negative sentence.
questions.explanation: 一般现在时否定句用 doesn't + 动词原形，主语 She 用 doesn't，因此 'She doesn't understand' 正确。
questions.evidence: She cannot understand fast English speech.

part1: Do you like learning English?
How often do you watch English videos?
What is difficult for you in English?
Do you have a teacher?
speaking.part2: Describe a skill you want to improve. You should say: what the skill is; why you want to improve it; how you plan to practice; and how you feel about it.
part3: Why do some people find listening difficult?
How can teachers help students with listening?
Is it better to listen to slow or fast English?
What advice would you give to a friend who wants to improve English?

transfer.writing: Write a short paragraph (about 80 words) about a skill you want to improve. Explain why it is important for you and what you will do to practice it.

materials.title: The Missing Skill: A Learner's Investigation
materials.instructions: 这是一份模拟英语学习材料，不是官方雅思考试。请先听/读对话，然后完成8道听力题。之后学习语法规则并做8道语法题。所有题目答案必须来自材料原文。听力部分有8道题，题型包括单选、填空和判断正误（True/False/Not Given）。填空答案必须与原文完全一致，且不超过字数限制。语法部分先看中文讲解，再完成8道新句子练习。最后有口语和写作任务。
materials.transcript:
Mia: Hi, Leo. You look worried. What's wrong?
Leo: I got my speaking test result. I'm stuck at 5.5. I don't know why.
Mia: Let's find out. When did you start preparing?
Leo: Three months ago. I practice every day.
Mia: Do you record yourself?
Leo: No, I don't. I just speak alone.
Mia: That's the problem. You need feedback. Have you tried a language partner?
Leo: I had one, but she moved away. Now I have no one to talk to.
Mia: I can help. We can meet twice a week. But first, tell me: what do you find difficult?
Leo: Long answers. I give short answers. The examiner asks 'Why?' and I say 'Because I like it.'
Mia: So you need to extend your answers. Also, your grammar—do you check your tenses?
Leo: Not really. I often mix past and present.
Mia: OK. Let's make a plan. You will record one answer daily. Then we will listen together and fix one grammar point each time.
Leo: That sounds good. But I'm shy about recording.
Mia: Everyone is at first. After a week, it gets easier. Trust me.
Leo: Alright. When do we start?
Mia: Tomorrow at 6 p.m. Bring your phone and a notebook.
Leo: Deal. Thanks, Mia.

questions.prompt: What is Leo's speaking test score?
questions.explanation: 原文中Leo说“I'm stuck at 5.5.”，所以答案是5.5。
questions.evidence: I'm stuck at 5.5.

questions.prompt: How often does Leo practice speaking?
questions.explanation: Leo说“I practice every day.”，因此频率是每天。
questions.evidence: I practice every day.

questions.prompt: Leo does not record himself. He just speaks ______.
questions.explanation: Leo说“I just speak alone.”，所以填alone。
questions.evidence: I just speak alone.

questions.prompt: Why did Leo stop having a language partner?
questions.explanation: Leo说“she moved away”，所以语言伙伴搬走了。
questions.evidence: I had one, but she moved away.

questions.prompt: What does Mia suggest Leo do daily?
questions.explanation: Mia说“You will record one answer daily.”，所以建议每天录一个回答。
questions.evidence: You will record one answer daily.

questions.prompt: True, False, or Not Given: Leo often mixes past and present tenses.
questions.explanation: Leo说“I often mix past and present.”，与题目一致，所以是True。
questions.evidence: I often mix past and present.

questions.prompt: True, False, or Not Given: Mia is a professional IELTS examiner.
questions.explanation: 原文没有提到Mia的职业，只说“I can help.”，所以无法判断她是否是考官，选Not Given。
questions.evidence: I can help.

questions.prompt: Mia and Leo will meet tomorrow at ______ p.m.
questions.explanation: Mia说“Tomorrow at 6 p.m.”，所以填6。
questions.evidence: Tomorrow at 6 p.m.

vocabulary.example: I'm stuck at 5.5.
You will record one answer daily.
You need feedback.
So you need to extend your answers.
do you check your tenses
But I'm shy about recording.
Bring your phone and a notebook.
Let's make a plan.

grammar.title: 基础时态、问句、名词数量和常见从句综合复习
grammar.explanation: 英语中，时态表示动作发生的时间。一般现在时表示经常性动作或事实，如“I practice every day.”；一般过去时表示过去发生的动作，如“She moved away.”；一般将来时表示将来，如“You will record one answer daily.”。问句需要助动词提前，如“Do you record yourself?”。名词数量要注意可数名词的复数，如“answers”。常见从句包括宾语从句（I think that...）和原因状语从句（because...）。本次重点复习这些基础点。
grammar.example: You will record one answer daily.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She go to school every day.
She goes to school every day.
She going to school every day.
answers: She goes to school every day.
questions.explanation: 一般现在时，主语She是第三人称单数，动词go要加es，所以选“She goes to school every day.”。
questions.evidence: She goes to school every day.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct question.
questions.explanation: 一般现在时问句，主语he是第三人称单数，助动词用does，后面动词用原形like，所以选“Does he like apples?”。
questions.evidence: Does he like apples?

questions.prompt: Choose the correct past tense sentence.
questions.explanation: yesterday表示过去，see的过去式是saw，所以选“I saw him yesterday.”。
questions.evidence: I saw him yesterday.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct future sentence.
questions.explanation: tomorrow表示将来，用will + 动词原形，所以选“They will come tomorrow.”。
questions.evidence: They will come tomorrow.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct plural form.
questions.explanation: box的复数是boxes，加es，所以选“three boxes”。
questions.evidence: three boxes

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence with a clause.
options: I think that he is right.
I think what he is right.
answers: I think that he is right.
questions.explanation: 宾语从句可以用that引导，且从句需要完整的主谓结构，所以“I think that he is right.”正确。
questions.evidence: I think that he is right.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct reason clause.
options: I stay home because it rains.
I stay home because it is raining.
answers: I stay home because it is raining.
questions.explanation: because引导原因状语从句，需要完整句子，所以“because it is raining”正确。
questions.evidence: I stay home because it is raining.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct negative sentence.
questions.explanation: 一般现在时否定，主语he是第三人称单数，用doesn't + 动词原形，所以选“He doesn't like coffee.”。
questions.evidence: He doesn't like coffee.

part1: Do you often practice speaking English?
How do you usually get feedback on your English?
What is difficult for you in English grammar?
Do you like recording yourself? Why or why not?
speaking.part2: Describe a time when you found a problem in your English learning and made a plan to fix it. You should say: what the problem was, how you found it, what plan you made, and how you felt about the plan.
part3: Why do some learners stay at the same level for a long time?
How can teachers help students find their weak points?
Is it better to study alone or with a partner? Why?
What advice would you give to someone who is shy about speaking English?

transfer.writing: Write a short paragraph (about 80-100 words) about a skill you want to improve. Describe the skill, why it is important for you, and two steps you will take to improve it. Use at least three different tenses.

materials.title: The Community Garden Plan: Changing Course After New Evidence
materials.instructions: 阅读下面的短文，回答8个问题。短文和问题均为英文，解释为中文。所有内容为模拟教学材料，不是官方雅思考试。请先通读全文，再做题。答案必须来自原文。
materials.passage:
Last month, the Green Street Community Group met to plan a new garden. They wanted to grow vegetables for local families. At first, they planned to use the small park behind the library. They thought the soil was good. They also believed the park was sunny all day.

However, a soil test showed a problem. The test found heavy metals in the soil. The group leader, Maria, said, “We cannot grow food here. It is not safe.” The members were surprised. They asked, “Are there other places?” Maria replied, “Yes, but we need to check them.”

Next, the group looked at two other sites. Site A was a empty lot near the school. Site B was a rooftop garden on the community center. The group tested both places. Site A had clean soil, but it was very small. Site B had strong sunlight and clean containers, but it was on the third floor. Some older members said, “We cannot climb stairs every day.”

Finally, the group chose Site A. They decided to use containers to add more space. They also planned to ask the school for help. The new plan starts next spring. Maria said, “We learned a lot. Good plans can change.”

questions.prompt: What did the group first plan to do?
options: Grow vegetables in the small park behind the library.
Build a rooftop garden on the community center.
Ask the school for help with containers.
Test the soil near the school.
answers: Grow vegetables in the small park behind the library.
questions.explanation: 原文第一段说他们最初计划使用图书馆后面的小公园。
questions.evidence: At first, they planned to use the small park behind the library.

questions.prompt: Why did the group NOT use the first park?
options: The park was on the third floor.
questions.explanation: 第二段说土壤测试发现重金属，因此不能种食物。
questions.evidence: The test found heavy metals in the soil.

questions.prompt: Which site had clean soil but was very small?
questions.explanation: 第三段明确说Site A土壤干净但很小。
questions.evidence: Site A had clean soil, but it was very small.

questions.prompt: What was a problem with Site B?
options: It was on the third floor.
answers: It was on the third floor.
questions.explanation: 第三段说Site B在第三层，一些年长成员说不能每天爬楼梯。
questions.evidence: Site B had strong sunlight and clean containers, but it was on the third floor.

questions.prompt: What did the group finally choose?
options: The small park behind the library
A new place near the library
questions.explanation: 最后一段说他们最终选择了Site A。
questions.evidence: Finally, the group chose Site A.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with ONE WORD from the passage: The group decided to use ______ to add more space.
questions.explanation: 最后一段说他们决定使用容器来增加空间。
questions.evidence: They decided to use containers to add more space.

questions.prompt: True, False, or Not Given: The group asked the school for help.
questions.explanation: 原文只说他们计划向学校求助（planned to ask），并没有说已经求助，因此不能判断为True。
questions.evidence: They also planned to ask the school for help.

questions.prompt: True, False, or Not Given: The new plan starts next summer.
questions.explanation: 原文说新计划明年春天开始，不是夏天，因此与原文矛盾。
questions.evidence: The new plan starts next spring.

vocabulary.example: They thought the soil was good.
The test found heavy metals in the soil.
It is not safe.
The members were surprised.
Next, the group looked at two other sites.
They decided to use containers to add more space.
We cannot climb stairs every day.
The new plan starts next spring.

grammar.title: 一般过去时与现在时综合复习：计划改变的表达
grammar.explanation: 英语中，谈论过去的计划或已完成的动作常用一般过去时（如 planned, thought, found, chose）。谈论现在的状态或普遍事实用一般现在时（如 is, are, have）。问句常把助动词提前，如 Did they plan? Are there other places? 名词数量要注意可数与不可数：soil 不可数，site 可数（two sites）。从句如 'They thought the soil was good' 中，宾语从句用陈述语序。
grammar.example: They thought the soil was good.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence about a past plan.
options: They planned to use the park.
They plan to use the park yesterday.
They are plan to use the park.
They planning to use the park.
answers: They planned to use the park.
questions.explanation: 过去计划用一般过去时 planned。
questions.evidence: At first, they planned to use the small park behind the library.

questions.prompt: Which question is correct?
options: Did the test find heavy metals?
Did the test found heavy metals?
Does the test found heavy metals?
The test did find heavy metals?
answers: Did the test find heavy metals?
questions.explanation: 一般过去时问句用 Did + 主语 + 动词原形。
questions.evidence: The test found heavy metals in the soil.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct noun form: There were two ______ near the school.
questions.explanation: two 后接可数名词复数 sites。
questions.evidence: Next, the group looked at two other sites.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the correct present tense?
questions.explanation: soil 不可数，谓语用 is。
questions.evidence: It is not safe.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct object clause: They believed ______.
questions.explanation: 宾语从句用陈述语序，过去时用 was。
questions.evidence: They also believed the park was sunny all day.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is correct about the final choice?
options: The group choose Site A yesterday.
The group did chose Site A.
questions.explanation: 过去选择用 chose（choose 的过去式）。
questions.evidence: Finally, the group chose Site A.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct question about ability.
options: Do we can climb the stairs?
questions.explanation: 情态动词 can 提前构成问句，后接动词原形。
questions.evidence: We cannot climb stairs every day.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses 'there are'?
questions.explanation: 复数 places 用 Are there...? 问句。
questions.evidence: Are there other places?

part1: Do you like gardens?
Is there a park near your home?
What vegetables do you like?
Do you often go outside?
speaking.part2: Describe a time when you changed a plan because of new information. You should say: what the plan was; what new information you got; how you changed the plan; and how you felt about the change.
part3: Why do plans sometimes change?
Is it good to change plans?
How do people get new information?
What can groups do when they have a problem?

transfer.writing: Write a short message (about 80 words) to a friend about a group plan that changed. Say what the first plan was, what problem happened, and what the new plan is. Use past tense for the first plan and present tense for the new plan.

materials.title: The Community Garden Plan: Revising After New Evidence
materials.instructions: 这是为B1水平学习者设计的原创模拟听力与语法练习（非官方雅思材料，场景与数据均为虚构）。请先听/读对话，注意说话人如何根据新证据修改计划。然后完成8道听力理解题（单选、填空、匹配、判断）。接着学习语法讲解并完成8道语法题。最后进行口语和写作迁移练习。所有题目答案必须来自材料原文。
materials.transcript:
Mia: Okay, everyone. Thanks for coming to the community garden meeting. We need to revise our plan for the spring planting day.
Ben: Why? What happened?
Mia: The city sent an email this morning. They will close the water tap in the garden next week for repairs.
Carla: Oh no. So we can't use the water tap on planting day?
Mia: Right. The tap will be off from Monday to Friday. Our planting day is next Saturday, so the tap will be back on. But we need a backup plan.
Ben: Wait, is planting day on Saturday? I thought it was on Sunday.
Mia: No, it's Saturday. I checked the calendar twice. Sunday is the rain date.
Carla: Okay. So what do we do about water?
Mia: We can ask the school next door. They have two big water tanks. I called them, and they said yes.
Ben: Great. How many tanks do they have?
Mia: Two. Each tank holds fifty liters. That's enough for our twenty small trees.
Carla: Do we still need volunteers to bring bottles?
Mia: Yes, but only ten bottles, not thirty. The tanks will do most of the work.
Ben: And what about the tools? Last time we had only five spades for twelve people.
Mia: Good point. The hardware store will lend us ten spades. I asked them yesterday.
Carla: Nice. So the new plan is: meet at nine, get water from the school, and start planting at ten?
Mia: Almost. Meet at eight thirty, because we need time to move the tanks.
Ben: Eight thirty is early, but okay. Who will bring the snacks?
Mia: I will. And Carla, can you send the new plan to everyone tonight?
Carla: Sure. I'll send it after dinner.

questions.prompt: Why does the group need to revise the plan?
options: The city will close the water tap next week.
The school said no to helping them.
The planting day moved to Sunday.
answers: The city will close the water tap next week.
questions.explanation: Mia说城市发来邮件，下周会关闭花园的水龙头进行维修，因此需要修改计划。
questions.evidence: The city sent an email this morning. They will close the water tap in the garden next week for repairs.

questions.prompt: When is the planting day?
questions.explanation: Mia明确说种植日是星期六，星期日是备用日期。
questions.evidence: No, it's Saturday. I checked the calendar twice. Sunday is the rain date.

questions.prompt: How many water tanks does the school have? (one word)
questions.explanation: Mia说学校有两个大水箱。
questions.evidence: Two. Each tank holds fifty liters.

questions.prompt: How many bottles do they need now?
questions.explanation: Mia说现在只需要十个瓶子，而不是三十个。
questions.evidence: Yes, but only ten bottles, not thirty.

questions.prompt: What time will they meet?
questions.explanation: Mia说八点半集合，因为需要时间移动水箱。
questions.evidence: Meet at eight thirty, because we need time to move the tanks.

questions.prompt: Who will send the new plan to everyone?
questions.explanation: Mia请Carla今晚把新计划发给大家，Carla答应了。
questions.evidence: And Carla, can you send the new plan to everyone tonight?

questions.prompt: Match the person to their task. Who will bring the snacks?
questions.explanation: Mia说她会带零食。
questions.evidence: I will. And Carla, can you send the new plan to everyone tonight?

questions.prompt: True, False, or Not Given: The hardware store will lend them ten spades.
questions.explanation: Mia明确说五金店会借给他们十把铲子。
questions.evidence: The hardware store will lend us ten spades. I asked them yesterday.

They will close the water tap in the garden next week for repairs.
But we need a backup plan.
They have two big water tanks.
Each tank holds fifty liters.
Do we still need volunteers to bring bottles?

materials.title: Choosing a Research Method for a School Garden Project
materials.instructions: 阅读下面的短文，回答10个问题。短文和问题均为英语，解释为中文。所有内容为模拟教学材料，不是官方雅思考试。请先通读全文，再做题。答案必须来自原文。
materials.passage:
Last month, a group of students at Greenfield Secondary School started a small research project. They wanted to find out how a school garden affects students' stress levels. The team leader, Mia, explained the plan to the class. "We need to choose a method," she said. "We can either give out a questionnaire or interview a few students." The group discussed the options for a week. In the end, they decided to use a questionnaire because it is quick and easy to collect many answers. Although questionnaires are useful, they cannot capture detailed personal stories. While interviews take more time, they provide deeper information. The students agreed to use both methods: a questionnaire for all 30 students and interviews with five volunteers. This mixed-method approach allowed them to gather both broad and deep information, which is important for a small-scale study.

After collecting the data, the team analyzed the results. They found that 70% of students felt calmer after spending time in the garden. However, because of the small sample size, the results may not apply to all students. Mia wrote in her report: "Although the garden seems to help, we need more data to be sure." The group also noted that while some students enjoyed gardening, others preferred just sitting quietly. Because the project was short, they could not observe long-term effects. The teacher, Mr. Chen, reminded them to be honest about limitations. He said, "Because of your careful work, the results are useful, but remember they are only a starting point." Being honest about limitations is an important part of any research, as it helps others understand how much confidence to place in the findings.

For the final presentation, the team created a poster with three sections: method, results, and conclusion. They used a topic sentence for each section. For example, the method section began: "We used a mixed-method approach to gather both broad and deep information." The results section started: "Most students reported feeling calmer after garden time." The conclusion stated: "While the garden may reduce stress, more research is needed." The team learned that a clear topic sentence helps the reader understand the main idea. They also practiced supporting sentences with reasons and examples. Mia said, "Because we planned carefully, our presentation was strong." The project taught them how to choose a method and how to write a clear argument. These skills will be useful in future studies and presentations.

materials.title: Choosing a Research Method: A Small Project Meeting
materials.instructions: 本材料为模拟教育练习，不是官方雅思考试，也不代表任何分数。先听/读对话，理解大意；再完成10道题（单选、填空、判断）。填空题答案必须来自原文，且不超过字数限制。语法部分先看中文讲解，再完成8道新句练习。最后进行口语和写作迁移练习。
materials.transcript:
Mia: Hi, everyone. Thanks for coming to our project meeting. We need to choose a method for our small research project on student study habits. Let's start with ideas.

Leo: I think we should use a questionnaire. It's fast, and we can get many answers. Because of the large number of students, a questionnaire is practical. It allows us to collect data from many people in a short time.

Mia: That's true. Although a questionnaire is quick, the answers may be short. We might not learn why students study in certain ways. We need to understand the reasons behind their habits.

Leo: Right. But we can add some open questions. While closed questions are easy to count, open questions give more detail. This way, we can get both numbers and explanations.

Mia: Good point. What about interviews?

Sara: Interviews are useful because we can ask follow-up questions. But they take a lot of time. Because of the time limit, we can only interview a few students. We have only two weeks for the whole project.

Mia: So, maybe we combine both? A short questionnaire for many students, and a few interviews for deeper information. This mixed method could give us a fuller picture.

Leo: I like that. Although it needs more planning, it gives us both width and depth. We can reach many students and still explore their reasons.

Sara: Yes. While the questionnaire gives us numbers, the interviews give us stories. Because we have two weeks, we should start the questionnaire this week. Then we can do the interviews next week.

Mia: OK. Let's decide: questionnaire first, then interviews with five volunteers. Sara, can you prepare the questions?

Sara: Sure. I'll send a draft by Friday. I'll make sure the questions are clear and short.

Leo: And I'll check the questionnaire for clear language. I'll also make sure the questions are not too difficult for students to understand.

Mia: Great. Thanks, everyone. Let's meet again next Monday to review the draft.

grammar.title: 主题句与支持句；although / while；because 与 because of
grammar.explanation: 主题句概括段落的中心论点，支持句用理由、例子或细节说明它；判断哪句适合作主题句，需要结合实际支持内容。although表示让步（虽然），后接完整从句。while可以表示同时发生（当……时），也可以对比两种情况（而/然而），不能把所有while都解释成让步。because后接完整从句；because of后接名词或名词短语，普通用法不直接接一个限定动词从句。
grammar.example: Although a questionnaire is quick, the answers may be short.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.

answers: Although the weather was cold, we went for a walk.
questions.explanation: although 后面接完整句子（the weather was cold），主句也是完整句子。

questions.explanation: 这里while表示两个动作同时进行，即“当我读书时，兄弟在做饭”。两边各有主语和有限谓语；不是把此处的while解释成虽然。

Interviews provide broad numerical coverage, while questionnaires explain a few individual cases.

materials.title: The Community Garden Meeting
materials.instructions: 阅读下面的短文，完成10道题目。题目类型包括单选、填空和判断正误/未提及。所有题目和选项均为英文，解释为中文。请仔细阅读短文，答案必须基于原文。本材料为模拟教育材料，不是官方雅思考试。
materials.passage:
Last Tuesday, the Maple Street Community Centre held a meeting about a new garden project. About forty people attended. The meeting was friendly, but people had very different ideas. The discussion showed how communities often need to balance different needs, such as safe places for children and support for local businesses. It also showed that when people listen to each other, they can often find a compromise that works for most of them.

A. The first speaker was Mrs. Chen, who has lived on Maple Street for thirty years. She said, "We need a garden because children have no safe place to play." She also said that the old parking lot behind the centre is ugly and dangerous. "Although the lot is small, we can grow vegetables and flowers there," she explained. Many parents agreed with her. They said the garden would give children a place to learn about nature and spend time outside. Some of them added that children today spend too much time indoors, and a garden would give them fresh air and exercise.

B. Next, Mr. Patel spoke. He owns a small shop on the corner. He said, "I understand the plan, but we need parking spaces because customers cannot stop here." He added, "While I like gardens, my business is important too." Some shop owners nodded. They said the parking lot is necessary because of the many cars on the street. Without parking, they worried that customers would go to other shops. Mr. Patel explained that many of his customers drive to the area, and if they cannot park nearby, they will simply shop somewhere else.

C. Then Ms. Rivera, a teacher, offered a solution. "We can use half the lot for a garden and half for parking," she said. "Because of the limited space, we must share." She suggested that the garden could have raised beds and that parking could be for short stays only. Most people liked this idea, but Mr. Patel was not sure. He wanted to know how the parking would be controlled. Ms. Rivera suggested that a simple sign could explain the rules, and that volunteers could help keep an eye on the lot.

D. Finally, the group voted. They decided to try Ms. Rivera's plan for six months. Mrs. Chen was happy because the children will have a garden. Mr. Patel agreed to wait and see. The meeting ended with tea and biscuits. Everyone promised to meet again in September to talk about how the plan is working. They also agreed to write down any problems during the trial period so that the next meeting could be more useful.

grammar.explanation: 在段落写作中，主题句（topic sentence）表达段落的主要观点，支持句（supporting sentences）提供细节、例子或原因来支持主题句。例如，主题句：'We need a garden because children have no safe place to play.' 支持句：'Although the lot is small, we can grow vegetables and flowers there.' 连接词 although 和 while 用于引导让步状语从句，表示对比或转折，后面接完整的句子（主语+谓语）。because 后面接从句（主语+谓语），而 because of 后面接名词或名词短语。例如：'Because of the limited space, we must share.' 中 because of 后接名词短语 the limited space。注意：although 和 while 不能与 but 连用。

materials.title: Community Consultation: The Library Garden Plan
materials.instructions: 这是一份原创模拟英语听力与阅读练习（非官方雅思试题，不用于分数换算）。先听/读对话，再完成10道题。听力部分注意不同说话人的自然轮换与自我更正。语法部分先看中文讲解，再做8道新句练习。所有题目选项均为英文，解释为中文。
materials.transcript:
Maya: Good evening, everyone. Thanks for coming to the community consultation about the library garden. I'm Maya, the project coordinator. We have three plans. Plan A is a quiet reading garden. Plan B is a children's play area. Plan C is a small vegetable garden. Please listen, then we vote.

Mr. Chen: Excuse me, Maya. I'm Chen Wei. I live next to the library. I support Plan A because I need a quiet place to read. But I'm worried about noise from children.

Maya: Thank you, Mr. Chen. That's a fair point.

Ms. Li: Hello, I'm Li Fang. I'm a mother of two. I prefer Plan B because my children have no safe place to play. Although the library is quiet, children need space too.

Mr. Chen: I understand, Ms. Li. But the garden is small. While I agree children need space, the noise could be a problem for readers.

Ms. Li: Maybe we can have quiet hours. Because of the small size, we can use times, not walls.

Maya: Good idea. Let's hear from Mr. Park.

Mr. Park: Hi, I'm Joon Park. I run the local food bank. I like Plan C because fresh vegetables help families. However, I know vegetables need care. Who will water them?

Maya: The library volunteers can help. They already work on Saturdays.

Mr. Park: That's good. But wait—I mean, I also worry about cost. Sorry, let me correct that. I worry about cost and time, not just water.

Ms. Li: I can organize a parent group for watering. Because we live close, we can take turns.

Mr. Chen: While I still prefer Plan A, I could accept Plan C if the vegetable garden is in the back corner. Then readers can be quiet in the front.

Maya: So, a mixed plan? Quiet reading in front, vegetables in the back, and children's play on Saturdays only?

Mr. Park: That sounds practical. Although it is not perfect, it is fair.

Ms. Li: I agree. Because of the schedule, children have a safe time, and readers have quiet times.

Maya: Great. Let's vote on the mixed plan. Please raise your hand. ... Thank you. The mixed plan passes with twelve votes. The next meeting is on June 15 at 6 p.m. Thank you all.

materials.title: The Library's New Map: Comparing Old and New Access
materials.instructions: 阅读下面的短文，完成10个问题。短文和问题均为英文，解释为中文。所有内容为模拟教学材料，不是官方雅思试题。请先通读全文，再作答。答案必须来自原文。
materials.passage:
A. The Westside Library is changing. Last year, the library had one main entrance and a single information desk. Today, it has three entrances and two help desks. The library is now more open and easier to enter. In the past, visitors walked to the back of the building to find the catalog. Now, a digital map stands near the front door. The map is more helpful than the old paper list. It shows every shelf and every room. If you compare the old building with the new one, you can see that the library wants to make things simple for visitors. The new entrances also mean that people do not have to walk through the whole building just to ask a question. This saves time, especially for people who visit the library for only a few minutes.

B. The number of visitors is growing. In January, about 1,200 people visited the library each week. In June, the number was 1,800. That is a 50 percent increase. The library also has more computers now. There were 10 computers before. There are 25 computers today. More people use the computers than before. The quiet room is smaller than the old reading room, but it is quieter. Many students study there. The staff say that students often come after school and stay for several hours. The extra computers help people who do not have a computer at home. They can check email, look for jobs, or do school work.

C. The library staff compared two plans. Plan A was cheaper, but Plan B was better for visitors. The staff chose Plan B. The new design has fewer shelves and more open space. There are more chairs and tables now. The children's area is larger than before. It has a new story corner. The library also added a small café. The café is busier in the morning than in the afternoon. The open space makes it easier for parents to watch their children while they read. The café gives visitors a place to rest and talk. It also sells drinks and simple snacks at low prices.

D. Not everything is perfect. The library has fewer parking spaces now. There were 40 spaces before. There are 30 spaces today. Some drivers are not happy. Also, the new map is sometimes difficult for older visitors. The staff now offers a short class every Saturday. The class teaches visitors how to use the digital map. The library plans to add more signs next year. The number of visitors continues to rise. The staff hope that the signs and the class will help everyone feel welcome. They also want to hear visitors' ideas, so they put a suggestion box near the front desk.

Mia: Hi, Ben. You look busy. What are you doing?

Ben: Yes. And the library now has a map near the door. It shows where everything is. So it’s easier to find things.

materials.title: The Community Survey: What the Numbers Really Say
materials.instructions: 阅读下面的短文，回答10个问题。文章和题目均为模拟材料，不是官方雅思试题。先读文章，再做题。填空题答案必须来自原文，且不超过字数限制。语法部分先看中文讲解，再完成8道新题。
materials.passage:
Last month, a group of volunteers in the town of Greenfield carried out a survey about local shopping habits. The group wanted to know how often people shopped in the town centre and what they thought of the local market. They printed 500 questionnaires and gave them out on a Saturday morning outside the main supermarket. By the end of the day, they had collected 320 completed forms.

A. The volunteers were pleased with the number of responses. However, when they began to analyse the data, they noticed several problems. First, most of the people who answered the survey were older residents. Only 18 per cent of the respondents were under 30 years old. The volunteers knew that younger people often shop online, so the survey may not represent the whole town.

B. Second, the questions were not always clear. One question asked, “How often do you visit the town centre?” The possible answers were “every day”, “once a week”, “once a month” and “rarely”. But some people said they visited twice a week, and others said they came only at Christmas. These answers did not fit the categories. As a result, the data for this question was less reliable than the volunteers had hoped.

C. Third, there was a problem with the time of day. The volunteers stood outside the supermarket from 9 a.m. to 12 p.m. People who work during the day were not there. There were very few responses from office workers. The group realised that the survey missed a large group of shoppers.

Despite these limitations, the survey produced some useful trends. For example, 65 per cent of respondents said they bought fresh food at the local market at least once a week. This was more than the number who bought fresh food at the supermarket (45 per cent). Also, there were more women than men in the sample: 60 per cent of respondents were women. The volunteers thought this might be because women do more food shopping in this town.

When the group presented their findings, they were careful to explain the limits. They said, “Our survey gives us a picture, but it is not a perfect photograph. We need more responses from younger people and from people who work full-time. Next time, we will use an online survey as well, and we will ask clearer questions.”

The group also compared their results with a similar survey from five years ago. In that survey, only 40 per cent of people said they bought fresh food at the local market once a week. So the new figure (65 per cent) shows an increase. However, the volunteers warned that the two surveys used different methods, so the comparison may not be completely fair.

In the end, the group learned an important lesson: numbers can tell a story, but we must always ask who gave the numbers and how they were collected. A survey is only as good as its questions and its sample.

materials.instructions: 本材料为原创模拟练习，不是官方雅思考试，也不代表任何分数。请先听/读对话，再完成10道题。听力部分注意不同说话人的自然轮换与更正。语法部分先用中文理解规则，再完成8道独立新句练习。最后完成口语与写作任务。
materials.transcript:
Mia: Okay, team, let's look at the weekend market survey. We collected 120 forms, but only 86 are complete. That's a problem because incomplete forms can affect the results.

Ben: Right. So the response rate is about 72 percent. But wait—most of those 86 came from the morning. The afternoon was quieter, so we have fewer responses from that period.

Mia: Exactly. There were more older visitors in the morning and fewer young people all day. So our sample is not balanced. This means we cannot easily generalise the findings to all visitors.

Ben: And there was one question about prices. Some people wrote 'cheap', some wrote 'too expensive'. The answers are not consistent, so it is hard to draw a clear conclusion about price opinions.

Mia: Good point. Also, the trend in the data is clear: sales went up after 11 a.m., then fell after 2 p.m. But we can't say why. We would need more detailed information to explain the reason.

Ben: Can we compare this with last year's survey? Last year we had 150 forms, so this year is smaller.

Mia: Yes, but last year's questions were different. We can't compare the two directly. That's a limit of this year's survey.

Ben: So what do we report? Maybe we say the survey shows a morning trend, but we need more data from the afternoon.

Mia: I agree. Let's write: 'There was a higher number of morning visitors, but the sample was small.' And we should mention the incomplete forms.

Ben: Okay. I'll make a simple chart: percentage of visitors by time of day. Morning 60 percent, afternoon 40 percent.

Mia: Wait, is that right? Let me check. Morning 52 forms, afternoon 34 forms. So morning is about 60 percent of the 86 complete forms. Yes.

Ben: Good. And we can add a note: 'There were 34 incomplete forms.' That's honest.

Mia: Perfect. Let's finish the report by Friday.

materials.title: Comparing Environmental Monitoring Methods: A Community Air-Quality Project
materials.instructions: 阅读一篇关于社区空气质量监测的短文，完成10道阅读理解题（单选、填空、匹配、判断正误/未提及）。然后学习语法：原因、结果与让步从句，以及 may / might / can 的语气差别。所有题目和选项均为英文，解释为中文。本材料为模拟教学材料，不是官方雅思考试，也不代表任何官方分数。
materials.passage:
A Community Air-Quality Project

[A] Last spring, the Greenfield Community Centre started a small air-quality project. The centre is near a busy road and a new building site. Many families wanted to know if the air was safe for children. The project leader, Ms. Chen, said, "We cannot test every street, so we must choose our methods carefully." The team compared three ways to monitor air quality: low-cost sensors, official monitoring stations, and simple dust traps.

[B] Low-cost sensors are small boxes that people can put on a balcony or a window. They are cheap, and they send data every minute. However, because they are cheap, they may not be very accurate. Ms. Chen explained, "The sensor is useful for showing changes during the day, but it might give a wrong number when the air is very wet." The team decided to use sensors in ten homes near the road. They put the sensors at the same height, so the results could be compared fairly.

[C] Official monitoring stations are large and expensive. They are very accurate, but there are only two stations in the whole town. One station is near the park, and the other is near the train station. Neither station is close to the new building site. Therefore, the team could not use station data to answer questions about the building site. Ms. Chen said, "Although the stations are excellent, they cannot tell us about our street."

[D] Simple dust traps are the third method. A dust trap is a box with a sticky surface. Dust sticks to the surface, and after one week, the team can see how much dust is in the air. Dust traps are very cheap, and anyone can make one. However, they only show the total dust for a week. They cannot show when the dust was high or low. The team used dust traps in five places: two near the road, two near the building site, and one in the community garden.

[E] After eight weeks, the team compared the results. The sensors showed that dust was highest between 7 and 9 in the morning, when many cars use the road. The dust traps near the building site were very dirty, but the trap in the garden was quite clean. The official station near the park showed low dust all month. Ms. Chen said, "Because the station is far from the road, its data does not describe our problem."

[F] The team also asked the families about the smell and noise. Some families said the air smelled bad in the evening. Others said they did not notice anything. Ms. Chen reminded everyone, "We may not have perfect data, but we can still take action. We can ask the town to water the building site road, and we can plant more trees near the school." The project report will go to the town council next month. The team hopes the council will support a second project with more sensors next year.

grammar.title: 原因、结果与让步从句；may / might / can 的语气差别
grammar.explanation: 英语中，原因从句常用 because / since / as 引导，说明“为什么”；结果常用 so / therefore 引出“所以”；让步从句常用 although / though / even though 引导，表示“虽然……但是……”。注意：although 不能和 but 同时使用；because 不能和 so 同时使用。情态动词 may / might / can 都表示“可能/能够”，但语气不同：can 表示一般能力或客观可能；may 表示较有把握的推测或允许；might 表示把握更小的推测。例如：The sensor can send data every minute.（能力）It may rain later.（较有把握）It might be wrong.（把握较小）。

questions.evidence: However, because they are cheap, they may not be very accurate.

materials.title: Comparing Environmental Monitoring Methods: A Community Science Project
materials.instructions: 本材料为原创模拟练习，不是官方雅思试题，也不对应任何官方分数。请先听/读对话，完成10道听力题；然后学习语法讲解，完成8道语法题；最后进行口语和写作迁移练习。听力部分包含自然对话、修正和干扰信息，答案不会直接读出。所有题目和选项均为英文，解释为中文。
materials.transcript:
Mia: Hi, Tom. Thanks for meeting me. I'm planning the community air-quality project for our neighborhood. We need to choose a monitoring method. Can you help me compare options?
Tom: Sure, Mia. I read about three methods: low-cost sensors, official monitoring stations, and citizen science kits. Each has strengths and weaknesses.
Mia: Let's start with low-cost sensors. They are cheap, so we can buy many. But are they accurate?
Tom: They are less accurate than official stations. However, if we use many sensors, we can see patterns across the neighborhood. The main problem is that they need regular calibration.
Mia: Right. Calibration takes time. What about official stations?
Tom: Official stations are very accurate. They are the gold standard. But they are expensive, and there are only two in our city. So we can't get detailed local data.
Mia: That's a big limitation. Citizen science kits might be a good middle ground. They are cheaper than official stations but more accurate than low-cost sensors.
Tom: Yes, but they depend on volunteers. If volunteers collect data consistently, the kits work well. If not, data quality suffers.
Mia: So the kits are reliable only if people are committed. Hmm. We also need to think about funding. The city may give us a small grant, but it might not be enough for official stations.
Tom: Exactly. We can apply for the grant, but we can't rely on it. Low-cost sensors are within our budget even without the grant.
Mia: True. But if we choose low-cost sensors, we must train volunteers to calibrate them. That could be a challenge.
Tom: Maybe we can combine methods. Use a few citizen science kits for accurate local readings, and many low-cost sensors for wide coverage. Although it's more complex, it might give us the best picture.
Mia: That's an interesting idea. But managing two systems might be too difficult for our small team.
Tom: You're right. We should consider our capacity. We have only five volunteers. So maybe we should start simple.
Mia: Let's think about the goal. We want to identify pollution hotspots. For that, wide coverage is more important than perfect accuracy. So low-cost sensors might be sufficient.
Tom: I agree. But we should still validate the sensor data with a few citizen science kits. That way, we can check the sensors' accuracy.
Mia: Good point. So the plan: buy twenty low-cost sensors, and use two citizen science kits for validation. We can apply for the grant to cover the kits.
Tom: That sounds practical. Even if the grant doesn't come through, we can still buy the sensors. The kits are optional.
Mia: Perfect. I'll write the proposal. Thanks for your help, Tom.
Tom: You're welcome. Let me know if you need more information.

grammar.title: 原因、结果与让步从句；may / might / can 的语气差别
grammar.explanation: 在英语中，我们可以用从句表达原因、结果和让步。原因常用 because, since, as；结果常用 so, so that；让步常用 although, even though, even if。注意：although/even though 不能和 but 同时使用。may / might / can 表示可能性时语气不同：can 表示一般能力或客观可能；may 表示较正式的可能性；might 表示可能性较小或更不确定。例如：We can buy sensors.（我们有能力买）The city may give us a grant.（可能给，较正式）It might not be enough.（可能不够，不确定性更大）。

questions.evidence: That way, we can check the sensors' accuracy.

questions.explanation: may 表示较正式的可能性，不确定。
questions.evidence: The city may give us a small grant.

questions.explanation: can 表示能力或客观可能，这里表示“我们可以申请”。
questions.evidence: We can apply for the grant, but we can't rely on it.

questions.explanation: might 表示可能性较小或更不确定。
questions.evidence: it might not be enough for official stations.

questions.explanation: 条件从句用 if 引导。
questions.evidence: if we use many sensors, we can see patterns across the neighborhood.

materials.title: The Office Energy Challenge
materials.instructions: 阅读下面的短文，完成10道题目。短文和题目均为英文，解释为中文。本材料为模拟教学材料，不是官方雅思试题。请先通读全文，再做题。答案必须来自原文。
materials.passage:
A. Greenfield Insurance moved to a new office last month. The building is old, and the electricity system is weak. On very cold days, the heaters use a lot of power. If everyone turns on a personal heater, the system may fail. So the company made a new rule: no personal heaters. The manager, Sarah, explained, "We must save energy because the system is old. If we don't save energy, we might lose power." Some workers were unhappy. They said, "We can wear warm clothes, but our hands are still cold." Sarah listened and then said, "You may use a small blanket at your desk. But you might feel cold near the windows." The workers agreed to try. This small change helped, but the company needed more ways to save energy.

B. The company also changed the lights. In the past, all the lights were on all day. Now, workers must turn off the lights in empty rooms. Tom, a worker, said, "I can turn off the lights when I leave a room. But I might forget." Sarah replied, "That's okay. We can put a note on the door." The company also bought new computers. The old computers used more electricity. The new computers use less. However, the new computers are slower. Some workers complained, "We can work faster with the old computers." Sarah said, "I understand. But we must use less energy. You may use the old computers for important jobs." The workers were not happy, but they understood. They knew saving energy was important for the whole company.

C. After one month, the company checked the electricity use. It was 20% lower. Sarah was happy. She said, "We saved energy because we worked together." But some workers still felt cold. One worker, Maria, said, "I wear two sweaters, but my feet are cold." Sarah said, "You can buy warm socks. The company will pay for them." Maria smiled. Another worker, John, said, "I might forget to turn off the lights, but the note helps." The company also started a new rule: on Fridays, workers can work from home. This saves energy because the office is empty. Some workers like this, but others don't. Tom said, "I can work at home, but I miss my friends." Sarah said, "You may come to the office if you want. But we must keep the lights off in empty rooms." Overall, the company saved energy, and most workers were happy with the changes. The experience taught everyone that small actions, like turning off lights and wearing warm clothes, can make a big difference.

questions.prompt: Why did the company make a new rule about heaters?
options: Because the electricity system is weak.
Because the heaters are too expensive.
Because the office is too hot.
Because the workers don't like heaters.
answers: Because the electricity system is weak.
questions.explanation: 原文第一段说“The building is old, and the electricity system is weak.”，因此公司制定规则是因为电力系统弱。
questions.evidence: The building is old, and the electricity system is weak.

questions.prompt: What can workers use at their desks?
questions.explanation: 原文中Sarah说“You may use a small blanket at your desk.”，所以工人可以用小毯子。
questions.evidence: You may use a small blanket at your desk.

questions.prompt: What must workers do in empty rooms?
questions.explanation: 原文第二段说“workers must turn off the lights in empty rooms.”，所以工人在空房间必须关灯。
questions.evidence: Now, workers must turn off the lights in empty rooms.

questions.prompt: How much lower was the electricity use after one month?
questions.explanation: 原文第三段说“It was 20% lower.”，所以用电量降低了20%。
questions.evidence: It was 20% lower.

questions.prompt: What will the company pay for?
questions.explanation: 原文第三段中Sarah说“The company will pay for them.”，这里的them指代前文的warm socks，所以公司会支付暖袜。
questions.evidence: You can buy warm socks. The company will pay for them.

questions.prompt: What is the new rule for Fridays?
options: Workers must stay in the office.
questions.explanation: 原文第三段说“on Fridays, workers can work from home.”，所以周五的新规则是可以在家工作。
questions.evidence: on Fridays, workers can work from home.

questions.prompt: Tom misses his friends when he works at home.
questions.explanation: 原文第三段中Tom说“I can work at home, but I miss my friends.”，明确表示他想念朋友，因此该陈述为True。
questions.evidence: I can work at home, but I miss my friends.

questions.prompt: The new computers are faster than the old computers.
questions.explanation: 原文第二段说“the new computers are slower.”，与陈述“新电脑更快”矛盾，因此为False。
questions.evidence: However, the new computers are slower.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with ONE WORD from the passage: The company also started a new rule: on Fridays, workers can work from ______.
questions.explanation: 原文第三段说“on Fridays, workers can work from home.”，所以填home。
questions.evidence: on Fridays, workers can work from home.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with ONE WORD from the passage: Sarah said, "You can buy warm ______."
questions.explanation: 原文第三段中Sarah说“You can buy warm socks.”，所以填socks。
questions.evidence: You can buy warm socks.

vocabulary.example: The building is old, and the electricity system is weak.
If everyone turns on a personal heater, the system may fail.
You may use a small blanket at your desk.
Some workers complained, "We can work faster with the old computers."
We must save energy because the system is old.
We must save energy because the system is old.
Now, workers must turn off the lights in empty rooms.
I can work at home, but I miss my friends.

grammar.title: 原因、结果与让步从句；may / might / can 的语气差别
grammar.explanation: 英语中，原因从句常用 because 引导，说明原因；结果从句常用 so 引导，说明结果；让步从句常用 although 引导，表示“虽然……但是……”。注意：because 和 so 不能同时用在同一个句子里；although 和 but 也不能同时使用。情态动词 may、might、can 都可以表示“可能”或“允许”，但语气不同：can 表示能力或较肯定的允许；may 表示允许或可能性，语气较正式；might 表示可能性较小或不确定。例如：You can work at home.（你可以在家工作——允许）You may use a small blanket.（你可以用小毯子——允许，较正式）It might rain later.（稍后可能会下雨——不确定）。
grammar.example: We must save energy because the system is old. If we don't save energy, we might lose power.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: The office is cold, ______ we wear warm clothes.
questions.explanation: 前半句是原因，后半句是结果，用 so 连接结果。
questions.evidence: The office is cold, so we wear warm clothes.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: ______ the new computers are slower, they use less electricity.
questions.explanation: 前后句是让步关系，用 Although 引导让步从句。
questions.evidence: Although the new computers are slower, they use less electricity.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: We turned off the lights ______ we wanted to save energy.
questions.explanation: 后半句是原因，用 because 引导原因从句。
questions.evidence: We turned off the lights because we wanted to save energy.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: I might forget to turn off the lights, ______ I will put a note on the door.
questions.explanation: 前半句是原因，后半句是结果，用 so 连接。
questions.evidence: I might forget to turn off the lights, so I will put a note on the door.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: You ______ use the old computer for important jobs. (permission)
questions.explanation: 表示允许，语气较正式，用 may。
questions.evidence: You may use the old computer for important jobs.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: It ______ rain later, so take an umbrella. (uncertain possibility)
questions.explanation: 表示不确定的可能性，用 might。
questions.evidence: It might rain later, so take an umbrella.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: She ______ speak three languages. (ability)
questions.explanation: 表示能力，用 can。
questions.evidence: She can speak three languages.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: ______ it was cold, they didn't turn on the heater.
questions.explanation: 前后句是让步关系，用 Although 引导。
questions.evidence: Although it was cold, they didn't turn on the heater.

part1: Do you like to save energy at home?
What do you do to save electricity?
Do you feel cold in winter?
Do you like to work from home?
speaking.part2: Describe a time when you had to change your habits to save energy. You should say: what the situation was, what you did, how you felt about it, and whether it was easy or difficult.
part3: Why do some people not want to save energy?
What can companies do to save energy?
Is it important for schools to teach children about saving energy?
How might energy use change in the future?

transfer.writing: Write a short email (about 100 words) to your manager suggesting one way to save energy in your office. Use because, so, although, and may/might/can.
