materials.title: The Office Energy Challenge
materials.instructions: 这是为B1–B2成人学习者设计的原创模拟听力材料（非官方雅思测试，也不代表任何分数）。先阅读中文语法讲解，再听/读对话，完成10道题。听力部分有自然的口语修正和干扰信息，答案不会直接读出。所有题目和选项均为英文，解释为中文。建议先做题，再看解释和证据。
materials.transcript:
Maya: Hi, everyone. Thanks for coming. As you know, the company has a new energy rule. We must cut electricity use by 20 percent this month. I know it's hard, but we can do it.
Tom: Sorry, Maya, can I ask something? Why this month? Is it because of the hot weather?
Maya: Good question. The main reason is that our energy costs went up a lot last year. So the company wants to save money. Also, the government may give a reward to green offices.
Tom: I see. So if we use less power, we might get some money back?
Maya: Exactly. But we don't have to do anything dangerous. We can still work comfortably.
Lisa: I have an idea. We could turn off the lights near the windows. The sun is very bright in the afternoon.
Maya: That's a great idea, Lisa. We can do that. But please don't turn off the lights in the hallway. It's dark there, and people might fall.
Tom: What about the air conditioning? Can we turn it off?
Maya: Hmm, we may not turn it off completely. It's very hot today. But we can set it to 26 degrees. That saves a lot of energy.
Tom: OK. And the printers? They use power when we are not using them.
Maya: Yes, they do. So we should turn them off at night. But wait—I mean, we can turn them off at night, but not during the day. Some people need to print.
Lisa: What about the coffee machine? It's always on.
Maya: Good point. The coffee machine can stay on during work hours. But we might turn it off after 6 p.m. Actually, let's turn it off after 6. It's not a big problem.
Tom: So, to sum up: lights off near windows, AC at 26, printers off at night, coffee machine off after 6. Is that right?
Maya: Yes, that's right. And one more thing: if we save energy, the company may give us a small bonus. But I'm not sure yet. It's only a possibility.
Lisa: Even if we don't get a bonus, it's good for the environment.
Maya: True. Although it's a small change, it can make a big difference. Thanks, everyone.

questions.prompt: Why does the company have the new energy rule?
options: Because energy costs went up last year.
Because the office is too cold.
answers: Because energy costs went up last year.
questions.explanation: Maya说主要原因是去年能源成本大幅上涨，所以公司想省钱。
questions.evidence: The main reason is that our energy costs went up a lot last year.

questions.prompt: What does Maya say about the government?
options: The government may give a reward to green offices.
The government will close the office.
The government already gave the company money.
answers: The government may give a reward to green offices.
questions.explanation: Maya用may表示可能性：政府可能给绿色办公室奖励。
questions.evidence: Also, the government may give a reward to green offices.

questions.prompt: What does Lisa suggest?
options: Turn off the lights near the windows.
answers: Turn off the lights near the windows.
questions.explanation: Lisa建议关掉窗户附近的灯，因为下午阳光很亮。
questions.evidence: We could turn off the lights near the windows.

questions.prompt: Why does Maya say people might fall?
options: Because the lights are too bright.
questions.explanation: Maya说走廊很暗，关灯可能让人摔倒。
questions.evidence: It's dark there, and people might fall.

questions.prompt: What temperature should the air conditioning be set to?
questions.explanation: Maya说把空调设为26度可以省很多电。
questions.evidence: But we can set it to 26 degrees.

questions.prompt: When can the printers be turned off?
questions.explanation: Maya说打印机可以在晚上关掉，但白天不行，因为有人要打印。
questions.evidence: So we should turn them off at night.

questions.prompt: When might the coffee machine be turned off?
questions.explanation: Maya说咖啡机可以在下午6点后关掉。
questions.evidence: But we might turn it off after 6 p.m.

questions.prompt: What does Maya say about the bonus?
questions.explanation: Maya用may表示可能，并说“I'm not sure yet. It's only a possibility.”
questions.evidence: But I'm not sure yet. It's only a possibility.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with one word from the talk: We must cut electricity use by ______ percent this month.
questions.explanation: Maya说本月必须减少20%的用电。
questions.evidence: We must cut electricity use by 20 percent this month.

questions.prompt: What is Lisa's opinion about the bonus?
options: Even without a bonus, saving energy is good for the environment.
The bonus is the most important thing.
The company will never give a bonus.
answers: Even without a bonus, saving energy is good for the environment.
questions.explanation: Lisa用even if表示让步：即使没有奖金，节能对环境也有好处。
questions.evidence: Even if we don't get a bonus, it's good for the environment.

vocabulary.example: We must cut electricity use by 20 percent this month.
Also, the government may give a reward to green offices.
We can still work comfortably.
But please don't turn off the lights in the hallway.
We may not turn it off completely.
But I'm not sure yet. It's only a possibility.
Even if we don't get a bonus, it's good for the environment.
Although it's a small change, it can make a big difference.

grammar.title: 原因、结果与让步从句；may / might / can 的语气差别
grammar.explanation: 原因从句用 because / since / as 说明理由，例如 because energy costs went up。结果从句用 so / that's why 说明结果。让步从句用 although / even if / though 表示“虽然、即使”，主句仍然成立。may 表示“可能”（较正式、可能性中等），might 表示“也许”（可能性稍低或更不确定），can 表示“能够/可以”（能力或许可），不是猜测。注意：may not 是“可能不”，can't 是“不能”。
grammar.example: Although it's a small change, it can make a big difference.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word: ______ the office is small, it uses a lot of power.
questions.explanation: 前后是让步关系：虽然办公室小，但用电多。用Although。
questions.evidence: Although it's a small change, it can make a big difference.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word: We turned off the lights ______ we wanted to save energy.
questions.explanation: 后面是原因，用because。
questions.evidence: The main reason is that our energy costs went up a lot last year.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word: It was very hot, ______ we opened the windows.
questions.explanation: 前面是原因，后面是结果，用so。
questions.evidence: So the company wants to save money.

questions.prompt: Which sentence shows a possibility, not an ability?
options: We can turn off the lights.
questions.explanation: might表示可能性；can表示能力或许可。
questions.evidence: But we might turn it off after 6 p.m.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word: The government ______ give us a reward, but I'm not sure.
questions.explanation: 表示不确定的可能性，用may。
questions.evidence: Also, the government may give a reward to green offices.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word: ______ we don't get the bonus, we will still save energy.
questions.explanation: 表示让步“即使”，用Even if。
questions.evidence: Even if we don't get a bonus, it's good for the environment.

questions.prompt: Which sentence means 'it is possible that we will not turn it off completely'?
options: We may not turn it off completely.
We can't turn it off completely.
We must not turn it off completely.
answers: We may not turn it off completely.
questions.explanation: may not表示“可能不”；can't表示“不能”；must not表示“禁止”。
questions.evidence: We may not turn it off completely.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word: She was tired, ______ she finished the report.
questions.explanation: 前后是让步关系：虽然累，但还是完成了报告。
questions.evidence: Although it's a small change, it can make a big difference.

Do you think small changes can help the environment?

materials.title: A Review of the Bridge Program: How One School Shared Its Resources
materials.instructions: 这是为成人英语学习者编写的原创模拟阅读材料（非官方雅思试题，也不代表任何真实学校或研究）。请先通读文章，理解大意；然后完成10道阅读题（单选、填空、匹配、判断正误/未提及）。所有题目和选项均为英文，解释为中文。语法部分先学习“条件句、数量词、段落间的指代与衔接”的新规则，再完成8道独立新句子的语法题。最后进行口语和写作迁移练习。建议用时：阅读15分钟，语法10分钟，口语/写作各10分钟。
materials.passage:
A Review of the Bridge Program: How One School Shared Its Resources

[A] Last September, Westfield Community School started a small education program called the Bridge Program. The program was for students who needed extra help with reading and maths. The school had a limited budget, so the head teacher, Ms. Chen, had to decide how to use the money and the teachers' time. She wanted to help as many students as possible without making classes larger for everyone else. This is a review of what the school did, what worked, and what did not.

[B] First, the school checked the needs of each class. Teachers filled in a short form about every student who was below the expected level in reading or maths. The forms showed that 48 students needed help. However, the school could only pay for two extra teachers. Ms. Chen decided to use a “small group” plan. Each extra teacher worked with groups of six students for 30 minutes, four times a week. The groups met in the library, so the normal classrooms did not become crowded. The school also bought 60 new reading books and 20 maths workbooks. These resources were shared among all the groups.

[C] After ten weeks, the school did a stage check. The check had three parts: a reading test, a maths test, and a short interview with each student. The results were mixed. In reading, 32 of the 48 students moved up one level. In maths, only 19 students moved up. The interview notes showed that many students liked the small groups because they could ask questions more easily. However, some students said they felt “different” when they left their normal class. Also, the two extra teachers were very tired because they taught many groups every day.

[D] The school made three changes for the next ten weeks. First, it moved the group lessons to the morning, when students were more awake. Second, it asked two classroom teachers to join the small groups for one session a week. This gave the extra teachers a short break and helped the classroom teachers understand the students' problems. Third, the school started a “reading buddy” plan: stronger readers read with weaker readers for 15 minutes, twice a week. The school did not buy any new materials for this plan; it used the books it already had.

[E] At the end of the second stage, the school checked again. This time, 41 students moved up in reading, and 33 moved up in maths. The interview notes were also better: fewer students said they felt “different”, and more students said they enjoyed the morning lessons. The head teacher was pleased, but she said the program still had a problem: the school could not help every student who needed it. Next year, she hopes to find more money for a third extra teacher. If the school gets more money, it will also buy more books for the reading buddy plan.

[F] In conclusion, the Bridge Program shows that a school can use limited resources in a better way. Small groups, morning lessons, and reading buddies all helped. However, the program also shows that stage checks are important: they help teachers see what is working and what is not. Without the checks, the school might not have changed the timetable or started the buddy plan. The school will continue the program next year and will review it again in December.

questions.prompt: How many students needed extra help at the start?
questions.explanation: 文章[B]段明确说“The forms showed that 48 students needed help.”，所以答案是48名学生。
questions.evidence: The forms showed that 48 students needed help.

questions.prompt: How long did each small group lesson last?
questions.explanation: 文章[B]段说“Each extra teacher worked with groups of six students for 30 minutes”，因此每次小组课30分钟。
questions.evidence: Each extra teacher worked with groups of six students for 30 minutes, four times a week.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of paragraph [C]?
options: The first stage check showed mixed results.
The school bought new books for the library.
The head teacher changed the timetable.
The reading buddy plan started in September.
answers: The first stage check showed mixed results.
questions.explanation: [C]段主要讲十周后的阶段检查结果有好有坏（阅读进步32人，数学进步19人，学生感受不同），因此主旨是“第一次阶段检查结果好坏参半”。
questions.evidence: The results were mixed.

questions.prompt: Which change was made for the second ten weeks?
options: Group lessons moved to the morning.
The school bought 60 new reading books.
The school hired a third extra teacher.
The library was closed for repairs.
answers: Group lessons moved to the morning.
questions.explanation: [D]段第一条变化是“it moved the group lessons to the morning”，即小组课改到上午。其他选项要么是之前的事，要么是明年才希望做的事。
questions.evidence: First, it moved the group lessons to the morning, when students were more awake.

questions.prompt: At the end of the second stage, how many students moved up in reading? Write the number and the word 'students'.
questions.explanation: [E]段说“41 students moved up in reading”，所以填“41 students”。
questions.evidence: This time, 41 students moved up in reading, and 33 moved up in maths.

questions.prompt: What did the school use for the reading buddy plan? Write FOUR WORDS from the text.
questions.explanation: 原文说“it used the books it already had”。答案books / it / already / had共四词，表示学校已经拥有的书；词数要求不包括原文the，因为答案本身已是完整的复数名词短语。
questions.evidence: The school did not buy any new materials for this plan; it used the books it already had.

questions.prompt: True, False, or Not Given: The classroom teachers joined the small groups every day during the second stage.
questions.explanation: 原文规定两位课堂教师每周加入一节小组课，而题目说every day（每天），频率直接矛盾，所以是False。不能把最初额外教师每周四次的小组课安排混到课堂教师后来每周一次的安排里。

grammar.explanation: 本课重点有三：1）条件句：表示“如果……就……”。真实可能发生用“if + 一般现在时，主句用 will/can + 动词原形”，例如“If the school gets more money, it will buy more books.”；谈现在或未来的想象、较不可能的情况，或与现实相反的情况，用“if + 过去式，主句用 would/could + 动词原形”，例如“If I had more time, I would join the group.”。2）数量词：可数名词用 many/few/a few，不可数名词用 much/little/a little；a lot of 两者皆可。3）段落间的指代与衔接：用 this/these/that/it/they 指代前文内容，用 however/therefore/also/first/second 等连接词使段落连贯。注意：本课新学“if 条件句（真实与虚拟）”，复习“数量词”和“指代衔接”。

materials.title: A Review of the 'Read to Succeed' Intervention
materials.instructions: 这是一份模拟的英语听力与阅读练习材料，主题为“资源分配与阶段检查”，语法重点为条件句、数量词以及段落间的指代与衔接。请先听或读一遍录音稿，然后完成10道题目。题目类型包括单选、填空和判断正误/未提及。所有题目和选项均为英文，解释为中文。请仔细阅读题目要求，答案必须基于原文。本材料不是官方雅思考试，也不代表任何分数等级。
materials.transcript:
Mia: Hi, Ben. Thanks for coming to the review meeting. Let's look at the 'Read to Succeed' program. It ran for six months in three primary schools.
Ben: Sure. I have the final report here. Overall, the results are positive, but there are some issues with resources.
Mia: Right. Let's start with the numbers. How many students took part?
Ben: We had 240 students in total. 120 in the experimental group and 120 in the control group. The experimental group received 30 minutes of extra reading practice every day.
Mia: And what about the teachers? Did they get any training?
Ben: Yes, but only 15 teachers were trained, and that was just for two days. Some teachers said they needed more support.
Mia: I see. So, what were the main findings?
Ben: Well, the experimental group improved their reading scores by 20 percent on average, while the control group improved by only 5 percent. That's a significant difference.
Mia: That's great. But did all students benefit equally?
Ben: Not exactly. Students who already had good reading skills improved less. The biggest gains were among students who started with lower scores.
Mia: Interesting. Now, about resources. Did you have enough books?
Ben: No, we didn't. We only had 200 books for 240 students. So some students had to share. Also, the books were not very interesting for older students.
Mia: That's a problem. What about the time? Was 30 minutes enough?
Ben: Most teachers said 30 minutes was too short. They wanted 45 minutes. But the school day is already full.
Mia: So, if we run the program again, what should we change?
Ben: If we have more funding, we should buy more books and train more teachers. Also, we could make the reading time longer, but only if we can find extra time in the timetable.
Mia: OK. And how about the assessment? Did you use the same test before and after?
Ben: Yes, we used the same reading test. But some teachers said the test was too easy for the older students.
Mia: I see. So, overall, would you recommend continuing the program?
Ben: Yes, definitely. But we need to fix the resource problems first. If we don't, the results might not be as good next time.
Mia: Agreed. Let's write a summary report and suggest some changes. Thanks, Ben.
Ben: You're welcome.

materials.title: The Missing Survey: A Team Learns to Check Its Data
materials.instructions: 阅读下面的短文，回答10个问题。文章和问题都是英语，解释是中文。所有内容为模拟教学材料，不是官方雅思考试。先读文章，再做题。做题时注意条件句、数量词和段落间的指代与衔接。
materials.passage:
A. The Brightline Marketing Team was excited. They had just finished a small survey about a new coffee shop, and the results looked great. Forty people answered the survey. Thirty-two said they would buy coffee there every week. The team leader, Maya, said, "If 80 percent of people say yes, then we should open the shop next month." Everyone agreed. They started to plan the opening.

B. But one team member, Leo, was not sure. He looked at the survey again. "Wait," he said. "We only asked people in our office building. And most of them are coffee drinkers already. If we ask people in other places, the answer might be different." Maya stopped. She looked at the numbers. "You are right," she said. "We have data, but it is not complete data."

C. The team decided to check their conclusion. They made a new plan. They would ask 100 people in three different places: the office building, a park, and a shopping center. They would also ask two questions: "Do you drink coffee?" and "Would you buy coffee here every week?" This time, they wanted a bigger and more varied group. They wanted to collect information from different types of people, not just office workers. They also wanted to represent the whole community better, so they chose places where many different people go.

D. The new results were very different. Of the 100 people, only 45 drank coffee. And of those 45, only 20 said they would buy coffee every week. That was just 20 percent of the whole group. Maya looked at the new numbers and said, "If we use only the first survey, we will make a mistake. The first group was too small and too special."

E. Leo added, "We also need to think about how many people walk by the shop each day. If only a few people pass by, even coffee drinkers will not stop." The team wrote a short report. They said: "Our first conclusion was too strong. We need more data from different places before we decide." They did not open the shop next month. Instead, they waited and collected more information. They also talked to a few coffee shop owners to learn about foot traffic. This helped them make a better decision about the shop.

F. In the end, the team learned an important lesson. A small number can tell you something, but it cannot tell you everything. When you make a conclusion, ask: Who did we ask? Where did we ask them? How many people answered? If the group is small or special, the result may not be true for everyone. Good decisions need good data, and good data need good questions. The team did not give up on the coffee shop idea. They just knew they needed to collect more information and represent all possible customers before making a final decision.

materials.title: The Missing Survey: A Team Challenges a Conclusion
materials.instructions: 这是一份原创的模拟英语听力与语法练习，适合B1–B2水平的成人学习者。请先听或读对话，然后完成10道听力理解题。之后学习条件句、数量词和段落衔接的新规则，并完成8道语法题。所有题目和选项均为英文，解释为中文。注意：对话中的人物会自然修正和插话，答案不会直接读出。请仔细根据原文作答。
materials.transcript:
Maya: Okay, everyone, thanks for coming. I want to talk about the new lunch menu. We sent a survey to 40 people last week, and 32 said they liked the menu. That's 80 percent. So I think we can say the menu is a big success.

Ben: Wait, Maya. You said 40 people got the survey, but how many actually answered?

Maya: Well, 32 people answered. That's the 80 percent.

Ben: Right, but that means only 32 out of 40 responded. And how many people work in this building?

Maya: About 200.

Ben: So we only heard from 32 out of 200. That's 16 percent. We can't say the menu is a success for everyone. If we want a real answer, we need more people to respond.

Maya: Hmm, I see your point. But the 32 people who answered were very positive. Almost all of them said they liked it.

Ben: Yes, but maybe the people who didn't like it didn't answer. That's a problem. If only happy people answer, the result is not fair.

Maya: Okay, that's a good point. So what should we do?

Ben: Let's send the survey again, but this time to all 200 people. And we can offer a small coffee coupon to people who finish it. If we get at least 100 answers, the result will be more reliable.

Maya: That sounds good. But we need to check the results at the end of the month, not just at the end. We should do a stage check every week.

Ben: Agreed. So, first, we send the survey to everyone. Second, we check how many people answer each week. Third, if we have enough answers, we look at the results together.

Maya: Perfect. And let's also ask one question about the price. Some people said the lunch is too expensive. If we don't ask about price, we might miss an important issue.

Ben: Good idea. So the new survey will have three parts: taste, price, and variety. And we will compare the answers from different groups, like people who eat lunch here every day and people who bring lunch from home.

Maya: Yes, that's better. So we are not saying the menu is a success yet. We are saying we need more data before we decide.

Ben: Exactly. And if the new results are different from the old ones, we will learn something important. That's the whole point of checking.

Maya: Thanks, Ben. I'm glad we talked. Let's start the new survey on Monday.

grammar.title: 条件句、数量词与段落衔接
grammar.explanation: 本课重点：1) 条件句：用 if 引导条件，主句用 will 或情态动词表示结果。例如：If we get more answers, the result will be reliable. 2) 数量词：表示数量的词如 all, some, most, none, 以及具体数字。注意区分整体和部分。例如：32 out of 200 表示部分。3) 段落间的指代与衔接：用 this, that, these, those, it, they 等指代前文内容，使段落连贯。例如：That's a problem. 中的 That 指代前一句的情况。新规则：条件句中 if 从句用一般现在时，主句用 will + 动词原形。

questions.explanation: 表示“在……之中”用 Of the people who answered。

materials.title: A City Weighs Three Public-Space Proposals
materials.instructions: 阅读下面的短文，完成10道题。短文和题目均为英文，解释为中文。本材料为模拟教学练习，不是官方雅思考试。请先通读全文，再做题。填空题答案必须来自原文，且不超过字数限制。
materials.passage:
A city council in the town of Riverton is considering three proposals for a new public space. The proposals were submitted by local groups, and they are being reviewed by a committee this month. The committee will decide which plan is chosen. Each proposal has strengths and weaknesses, and residents have been invited to share their opinions.

Proposal A: A Community Garden
This plan would turn an empty lot near the library into a community garden. The garden would be divided into small plots, and each plot would be rented to a family for a small fee. The money collected would be used to buy tools and seeds. Volunteers would take care of the shared areas. The garden would provide fresh vegetables and a quiet place to relax. However, some residents worry that the garden would attract insects and require a lot of water. Also, the lot is small, so only about twenty families could have plots.

Proposal B: A Children's Playground
This proposal suggests building a playground on the same empty lot. The playground would include swings, slides, and a climbing frame. It would be designed for children aged three to twelve. The equipment would be made of safe materials, and a soft surface would be installed under the play areas. Parents have supported this idea because the town currently has no playground. The council has received many letters in favor of the playground. On the other hand, the playground would be noisy, and it would not be open in the evening. Some older residents have said that they prefer a quieter space.

Proposal C: A Small Park with Benches
A third group wants to create a small park with trees, flowers, and benches. This plan would cost more than the other two because trees and benches are expensive. The park would be open to everyone at all times. It would provide shade in summer and a place for people to sit and talk. The group argues that a park would make the neighborhood more beautiful and would increase property values. However, the council must consider the cost. The city budget is limited, and the park would require ongoing maintenance.

The committee will hold a public meeting next week. At the meeting, residents can ask questions and express their views. The committee will then make a recommendation to the council. The final decision is expected by the end of the month. The chosen project will be funded by the city, and work will begin in the spring.

grammar.title: 被动语态；因果表达；分词作定语的基础辨认
grammar.explanation: 本课重点：1) 被动语态：be + 过去分词，强调动作承受者。例如：The proposals were submitted. 2) 因果表达：because, so, therefore, as a result 等。例如：because trees and benches are expensive. 3) 分词作定语：单个分词放在名词前，如 the chosen project；分词短语放在名词后，如 the money collected。辨认时先找名词，再看分词修饰谁。

materials.transcript:
Maya: Good evening, everyone. I'm Maya Chen, and I'm chairing tonight's meeting about the old train station site. We have three proposals for the empty land. First, can the planning team tell us what was found in the public survey?

Daniel: Yes. Last month, 1,200 residents were asked about the site. Most people said they wanted more green space. A smaller group asked for a sports center. Only a few people wanted shops.

Maya: Thank you, Daniel. So the survey shows strong support for a park. Now, let's hear the proposals. Anna, you're first.

Anna: My group proposes a community garden. The garden would be built by local volunteers. It would include raised beds, a small tool shed, and a seating area. The cost is low because the work would be done by residents. Also, fresh vegetables would be grown and shared.

Maya: Thanks, Anna. Any questions for Anna?

Daniel: I have one. Who would take care of the garden in winter?

Anna: Good question. A volunteer group would manage it. The city would provide water and tools.

Maya: OK. Next is Ben.

Ben: Our proposal is a sports center. It would be designed for young people. We would have a basketball court, a climbing wall, and a small café. The building would be paid for by a private company. But the company would also run the café and keep the profits.

Maya: Thank you, Ben. And the third proposal?

Priya: I'm Priya. My team suggests a quiet reading park. It would have trees, benches, and a small open-air library. Books would be donated by residents. The park would be maintained by the city parks department. The cost is medium, but the space would be open to everyone, all day.

Maya: Thank you, Priya. Now, before we vote, I want to remind everyone that the final decision will be made by the city council next month. Public comments can be sent by email until Friday. Thank you for coming.

materials.title: The Bridge, the Budget, and the Bus Lane
materials.instructions: 阅读一篇关于城市交通基础设施取舍的模拟教学材料（非官方雅思试题，非真实研究）。先通读全文，理解大意；再完成10道阅读题（单选、填空、匹配、判断）。填空题答案必须来自原文，且不超过字数限制。之后学习语法：被动语态、因果表达、分词作定语的基础辨认。语法部分有8道独立新句练习。最后完成口语和写作迁移任务。所有题目和选项均为英文，解释为中文。
materials.passage:
A city council in the town of Riverton met on Tuesday to discuss a major transport problem. The old North Bridge, which carries about 20,000 vehicles every day, is narrow and in poor condition. Engineers say it must be repaired or replaced within five years. The council has two main options, and each one has serious costs and benefits. This is a difficult trade-off between cost, time, and the environment.

Option A is to repair the existing bridge. This would cost about £8 million and take 18 months. During the work, the bridge would be closed to cars, and traffic would be sent through the town centre. Local shop owners are worried because customers might avoid the area. However, the repair would keep the bridge in its current location, so bus routes would not change. The council's transport officer, Maria Chen, said, "If we repair the bridge, we can keep the bus lane open. That means people who do not drive can still travel easily." Repairing the bridge would also mean less disruption to the existing road infrastructure, because no new roads would need to be built.

Option B is to build a new bridge 500 metres downstream. This would cost £22 million and take three years. The new bridge would have four lanes, a separate bus lane, and a wide path for bicycles and pedestrians. Because it would be built away from the town centre, traffic would not pass through local streets. But the new bridge would require a new road, and some green space would be lost. A local environmental group, Green Riverton, has opposed the plan. Its chair, David Okafor, argued, "The new road would cut through a park that is used by families every weekend. We should not destroy green space for cars." The group believes that building new infrastructure for cars goes against the town's environmental goals.

The council also considered a third idea: a temporary ferry service during the repair work. This was rejected because it would cost £3 million and carry only 500 people per day. The council will vote next month. Maria Chen added, "We need to think about the long term. A repaired bridge is cheaper now, but a new bridge may serve the town better in 30 years." The decision is not easy, and both sides have strong arguments. Some residents support the repair because it is cheaper and faster, while others oppose it because of traffic problems in the town centre. In the end, the council must weigh the short-term costs against the long-term needs of the town.

materials.title: The Bridge That Waited: A Lecture on Infrastructure Trade-offs
materials.instructions: 本材料为模拟教学练习，非官方雅思试题。听录音前先读题；录音中说话者会自然修正和插话，注意区分事实与干扰信息。语法部分先看中文讲解，再做8道新题。所有题目答案均来自原文，填空答案必须与原文完全一致。
materials.transcript: LECTURER: Good morning. Today we look at a small bridge project. It is a simulated case, not a real place. The town of Riverton wanted a new footbridge over the river. Two plans were discussed. Plan A was cheaper. Plan B was stronger. The council chose Plan B. Why? Because the river floods every spring. A weak bridge would be closed for weeks. So the stronger design was selected. The extra cost was about two million. That money came from the regional budget. Now, a trade-off means you gain one thing and lose another. Here, the town gained safety but lost some parkland. Three old trees were removed. Some residents were unhappy. They said the trees were important. The council agreed to plant ten new trees nearby. Those trees will grow slowly. So the benefit is delayed. MAYA: Excuse me, was the public consulted? LECTURER: Yes, two meetings were held. But only forty people came. MAYA: So most people were not heard. LECTURER: That is a fair point. The process was criticized for that reason. Now, look at the timeline. The design was finished in March. Construction started in June. The bridge was opened in December. It was used by 800 people on the first day. That number was higher than expected. The old ferry was closed afterwards. Some ferry workers were retrained. Others were let go. This is another trade-off. Jobs were lost, but travel time was cut. Before, the crossing took twenty minutes. Now it takes four minutes. The saved time helps local shops. Deliveries are faster. However, the bridge is not perfect. It was built for walkers and cyclists only. Cars cannot use it. So drivers still use the old road bridge. That bridge is often crowded. A wider road bridge was proposed, but it was rejected. The cost was too high. So the problem was only partly solved. Let me finish with a question. When you read about infrastructure, ask: who gains, who loses, and who decides? These three questions are useful. They are not always easy to answer. But they help you read critically. Next week we will look at a water project. Please read the short case before class. Thank you.

materials.title: The Museum of Uncertain Things
materials.instructions: 阅读一篇关于博物馆如何解读不确定证据的短文，完成10道阅读理解题（单选题、填空题、标题匹配题、判断题）。所有题目和选项均为英文，解释为中文。注意：本材料为模拟教学材料，不是官方雅思试题。
materials.passage:
A. The Museum of Uncertain Things is a small museum in a quiet town. It opened last year. The museum shows objects that are not fully understood. For example, there is a broken stone with strange marks. Nobody knows who made it or what the marks mean. The museum does not say, "This is a message from ancient people." Instead, it says, "We are not sure. Here are three possible ideas." Visitors can read the ideas and think for themselves.

B. The museum's director, Dr. Chen, explains the museum's rule. "We must be honest," she says. "If we do not know, we say we do not know. We can show what we think, but we must not pretend." The museum uses a simple system. Each object has a label with three parts: "What we see," "What we think," and "What we do not know." For the broken stone, the label says: "What we see: marks on stone. What we think: maybe a map, maybe a game, maybe art. What we do not know: who made it and why." This system helps visitors understand that evidence can be uncertain.

C. One day, a school group visited the museum. A boy named Leo asked, "Why don't you just guess? It would be easier." Dr. Chen smiled. "Guessing is easy," she said, "but it is not honest. If we guess, people may believe us. Then they will be wrong. We want people to think, not just believe." Leo thought about this. He said, "So you are teaching people to be careful?" Dr. Chen nodded. "Yes. And we are teaching them that it is okay to say 'I don't know.'"

D. The museum also has a room called the "Question Room." In this room, visitors can write their own ideas about the objects. They can write questions, too. The museum puts some of these notes on the wall. One note says, "Maybe the marks are a calendar." Another says, "I think it is a child's drawing." Dr. Chen says that these notes are important. "They show that people are thinking," she says. "That is what we want."

E. Not everyone likes the museum. Some people say it is too negative. They want clear answers. They say, "A museum should tell us the truth, not just ask questions." Dr. Chen understands this. "We do tell the truth," she says. "The truth is that we do not always know. That is a real answer, too." She believes that if people learn to accept uncertainty, they will be better thinkers. "In science, we often do not know," she says. "But we can still explore. That is the most important thing."

F. The museum is now planning a new exhibit. It will show objects from the ocean. Dr. Chen says, "We will use the same system. We will show what we see, what we think, and what we do not know." She hopes that more museums will follow this idea. "If we all pretend to know everything," she says, "we will never learn. But if we say 'we are not sure,' we can start a real conversation."

grammar.explanation: 英语中，一个句子可以充当另一个句子的主语、宾语或表语，这叫名词性从句。本课重点：1) that 从句作宾语或表语，that 常可省略，但正式文体常保留。例如：She believes that people can learn. 2) 情态动词 must, can, may, should 后接动词原形，表示义务、能力、可能性或建议。3) 条件句：if + 一般现在时，主句用 will/can/must 等。例如：If we guess, people may believe us. 注意：条件从句中不用 will。

materials.title: The Museum of Uncertain Evidence
materials.instructions: 这是一份为B1–B2学习者设计的英语听力与语法练习，主题为科技、隐私与观点组织。场景为虚构的博物馆策展会议，所有内容均为模拟教学材料，并非真实事件或官方考试。请先听录音（或阅读文字稿），然后完成10道听力题；接着学习名词性从句（that从句）与情态动词条件表达，并完成8道语法题；最后进行口语和写作迁移练习。听力题中，A0/A1题目使用简短英语，答案可直接从原文找到；A2+题目包含推断和NOT GIVEN。所有题目答案均可在原文中找到证据，NOT GIVEN题会说明缺失信息。
materials.transcript:
Museum director Anna: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for coming to this early meeting. We need to decide how to present the new exhibition about the ancient water clock. As you know, the clock is broken, and we have only a few pieces.

Curator Ben: Right. The problem is that we don't know exactly how the clock worked. Some parts are missing. We have a drawing from 1890, but it may be wrong.

Anna: So we must be careful. We can't say 'this is how it worked' if we are not sure. Maybe we should show the drawing and the real pieces side by side.

Ben: I agree. But visitors might think the drawing is a photo of the real clock. We need a clear label.

Education officer Chen: I have an idea. We can put a question mark on the label. For example: 'How did the water flow? We are not sure.' That way, visitors know that the evidence is uncertain.

Anna: That's good. But we also need to think about privacy. Some of the letters we found mention a family name. We should not show the full name without permission.

Ben: True. The letters are from a private collection. The owner said we can show them, but we must hide the name.

Chen: So we can cover the name with a black line. And we can explain that we are protecting privacy.

Anna: Perfect. Now, about the technology. We want to add a small screen that shows a 3D model. But the model is only a guess. We must tell visitors that it is a reconstruction, not the real thing.

Ben: I can write a short text for the screen. Something like: 'This model is based on our best ideas, but it may not be correct.'

Chen: And we can ask visitors what they think. Maybe a small voting station: 'Do you think the water flowed from the top or the bottom?'

Anna: I like that. It makes people think about evidence. But we must not say that one answer is right. We don't know.

Ben: So the exhibition is about questions, not answers.

Anna: Exactly. Let's also remember that some visitors may not read English well. We should use simple words and maybe pictures.

Chen: I can make a simple guide with short sentences. And we can train the staff to say: 'We are not sure, but here is what we know.'

Anna: Good. So to summarize: we will show the real pieces, the old drawing with a question mark, the letters with the name hidden, and the 3D model with a clear warning. Any questions?

Ben: Just one. When do we need the final text?

Anna: By Friday, please. Thank you, everyone.

materials.title: The Community Garden Debate: Privacy, Technology, and Social Change
materials.instructions: 阅读下面的短文，回答10个问题。问题类型包括单选、填空、匹配（用单选形式）和判断正误/未提及。填空题答案必须来自原文，且不超过字数限制。所有问题用英语作答。语法部分先看中文讲解，再完成8道新题。口语和写作任务为模拟练习，不是官方雅思考试。
materials.passage:
A. In the small town of Riverton, a community garden was created five years ago. At first, only ten families used it. They grew vegetables and shared tools. Last year, the town council decided to add new technology: a website where people could book garden plots online, and a camera to watch the garden at night. The council said this would help more people use the garden safely. However, some gardeners were not happy. They worried that the camera would record their faces and that their personal information might be shared. Maria, a gardener for three years, said, “I think that the camera is a good idea for safety, but I am not sure that everyone understands how the website works.”

B. The council organized a meeting to discuss the changes. At the meeting, Tom, a council member, explained, “We believe that the website will make booking easier. The camera will only record when there is movement at night. We will not share your information with anyone.” Some gardeners asked questions. “What happens if the camera records my children playing?” asked one parent. Tom replied, “The camera only works at night, so it will not record children during the day.” Another gardener, Ahmed, said, “I think that we need a clear rule about who can see the recordings. If we don’t have a rule, people will worry.” The council agreed to write a privacy policy.

C. After the meeting, the council wrote a policy. It said that only the garden manager could see the recordings, and only if there was a problem, such as a theft. The recordings would be deleted after seven days. The policy also said that the website would not ask for more information than necessary: just a name and an email address. When gardeners read the policy, most felt better. Maria said, “Now I understand that the council listened to us. I think that the policy is fair.” Ahmed added, “If the council keeps its promise, we can trust the technology.” The garden now has fifty families, and the website is used every day. The council plans to add more gardens in other parts of town, but they promise to ask the community first.

D. This story shows how technology can change a community. It also shows that people need to talk about privacy and rules. When people discuss their worries and listen to each other, they can find solutions that work for everyone. The gardeners in Riverton learned that new technology is not just about machines; it is also about people and their trust.

grammar.title: 名词性从句入门：that 从句与情态动词/条件表达
grammar.explanation: 英语中，有些动词后面可以跟一个由 that 引导的句子，这个句子整体充当动词的宾语，叫做宾语从句。例如：I think that the camera is a good idea. 这里 that 没有实际意思，只起连接作用，口语中常省略。注意从句要用陈述语序，即使原句是疑问句，变成从句时也要用陈述语序，如：What does he want? → I don't know what he wants. 另外，情态动词（can, could, will, would, should, might 等）表示可能性、能力、建议等；条件句用 if 引导，表示“如果……”。例如：If we don't have a rule, people will worry. 条件句主句常用 will 或情态动词。
grammar.example: I think that the camera is a good idea for safety, but I am not sure that everyone understands how the website works.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I think that she is right.
I think that is she right.
answers: I think that she is right.
questions.explanation: 宾语从句要用陈述语序，且不能省略系动词。A选项语序正确，B选项是疑问语序，C选项缺少系动词。
questions.evidence: I think that the camera is a good idea for safety

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: He said that he would come.
He said that would he come.
He said that he will come yesterday.
answers: He said that he would come.
questions.explanation: 宾语从句用陈述语序，且主句是过去时，从句常用过去将来时would。A正确，B语序错误，C时态不一致。
questions.evidence: The council said this would help more people use the garden safely.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: If it rains, we will stay at home.
If it will rain, we stay at home.
If it rains, we would stay at home.
answers: If it rains, we will stay at home.
questions.explanation: 条件句：if 从句用一般现在时，主句用一般将来时（will）。A正确，B从句用了will，C主句用了would（与现在事实相反时用）。
questions.evidence: If we don’t have a rule, people will worry.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She might be at home now.
She might is at home now.
answers: She might be at home now.
questions.explanation: 情态动词might后接动词原形，be是原形。A正确，B用了is，C缺少动词。
questions.evidence: their personal information might be shared

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I don't know what he wants.
I don't know what does he want.
I don't know what he want.
answers: I don't know what he wants.
questions.explanation: 宾语从句用陈述语序，且主语he是第三人称单数，动词用wants。A正确，B是疑问语序，C动词形式错误。
questions.evidence: I am not sure that everyone understands how the website works.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The teacher said that the earth goes around the sun.
The teacher said that the earth went around the sun.
The teacher said that does the earth go around the sun.
answers: The teacher said that the earth goes around the sun.
questions.explanation: 宾语从句表示客观真理时，即使主句是过去时，从句仍用一般现在时。A正确，B时态错误，C语序错误。
questions.evidence: We believe that the website will make booking easier.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: If you study hard, you can pass the exam.
If you study hard, you could pass the exam.
If you will study hard, you can pass the exam.
answers: If you study hard, you can pass the exam.
questions.explanation: 条件句if从句用一般现在时，主句用情态动词can表示能力。A正确，B用了could（表示可能性较小或虚拟），C从句用了will。

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I am not sure that he will join us.
I am not sure that will he join us.
I am not sure that he joins us tomorrow.
answers: I am not sure that he will join us.
questions.explanation: 宾语从句用陈述语序，且表示将来用will。A正确，B语序错误，C时态错误。

materials.title: Comparing Explanations of Social Change: A Student Discussion
materials.instructions: 本材料为模拟教学练习，不是官方雅思考试。请先听/读对话，理解大意；然后完成10道听力题（题型混合：单选、填空、判断正误/未提及）。填空答案必须与原文完全一致，且不超过字数限制。之后学习名词性从句（that从句）和情态动词条件表达，完成8道语法题。最后进行口语和写作迁移练习。所有题目和选项均为英文，解释为中文。
materials.transcript:
Mia: Hi, Leo. Did you finish the reading for sociology? I'm still confused about the two explanations of social change.
Leo: Hey, Mia. Yes, I read both. One says technology drives change. The other says social movements do. What do you think?
Mia: I think technology is important, but it can't explain everything. For example, the internet changed how we shop, but people also organized online to protest. So maybe both matter.
Leo: That's a good point. The first article argues that new tools create new behaviors. It says the smartphone changed family life. But the second article says that's too simple. It argues that people choose how to use technology.
Mia: Right. The second one gives the example of remote work. It became common not just because of laptops, but because workers demanded flexibility. So social pressure played a role.
Leo: Exactly. So the two explanations are not completely separate. One focuses on things, the other on people. I think a better explanation combines them.
Mia: I agree. But the exam question asks us to compare, not combine. We need to say what each explanation claims and what evidence it uses.
Leo: True. Let's make a table. Column A: technology explanation. Column B: social movement explanation. Then we can see the differences.
Mia: Good idea. For column A, the key claim is that technology causes change directly. Evidence: the internet and smartphones. For column B, the claim is that collective action causes change. Evidence: labor movements and online campaigns.
Leo: But wait, the second article also mentions that technology can help movements. So it's not either-or. The authors might actually agree more than they think.
Mia: Maybe. But for the exam, we should present them as separate first, then maybe mention the overlap in a conclusion. That shows deeper understanding.
Leo: Okay. So our answer structure: introduction, explanation A, explanation B, comparison, conclusion. Does that sound right?
Mia: Yes. And we must use our own words, not copy sentences. The teacher said paraphrasing is important.
Leo: Got it. Let's start writing the introduction now. We can say that social change is complex and different theories highlight different causes.
Mia: Perfect. I'll write the first part, you write the second, and then we'll compare.

questions.prompt: What are Mia and Leo mainly doing?
options: Preparing for a sociology exam by comparing explanations
Arguing about which explanation is correct
Reading a new article about smartphones
answers: Preparing for a sociology exam by comparing explanations
questions.explanation: 对话开头Mia说“I'm still confused about the two explanations of social change”，Leo回应并讨论如何比较两种解释，最后Mia说“the exam question asks us to compare”，说明他们在准备考试并比较解释。
questions.evidence: Mia: Hi, Leo. Did you finish the reading for sociology? I'm still confused about the two explanations of social change.

questions.prompt: According to the first article, what changed family life?
questions.explanation: Leo说“The first article argues that new tools create new behaviors. It says the smartphone changed family life.” 直接指出智能手机改变了家庭生活。
questions.evidence: Leo: That's a good point. The first article argues that new tools create new behaviors. It says the smartphone changed family life.

questions.prompt: What does the second article argue about technology?
options: Technology always causes social change directly.
People choose how to use technology.
Technology is not important at all.
answers: People choose how to use technology.
questions.explanation: Leo提到第二篇文章说第一种解释太简单，并说“It argues that people choose how to use technology.” 因此第二篇文章认为人们选择如何使用技术。
questions.evidence: But the second article says that's too simple. It argues that people choose how to use technology

questions.prompt: Why did remote work become common, according to the second article?
questions.explanation: Mia说“It became common not just because of laptops, but because workers demanded flexibility.” 说明远程工作普及不仅因为笔记本电脑，还因为工人要求灵活性。
questions.evidence: Mia: Right. The second one gives the example of remote work. It became common not just because of laptops, but because workers demanded flexibility.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with ONE WORD from the transcript: The second article gives the example of ______ work.
questions.explanation: Mia说“The second one gives the example of remote work.” 因此填入remote。
questions.evidence: Mia: Right. The second one gives the example of remote work.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with ONE WORD from the transcript: Leo suggests making a ______ to compare the two explanations.
questions.explanation: Leo说“Let's make a table.” 因此填入table。
questions.evidence: Leo: True. Let's make a table.

questions.prompt: What is the key claim of the technology explanation (Column A)?
questions.explanation: Mia说“For column A, the key claim is that technology causes change directly.” 直接给出技术解释的核心主张。
questions.evidence: Mia: Good idea. For column A, the key claim is that technology causes change directly.

questions.prompt: What evidence does the social movement explanation use?
questions.explanation: Mia说“For column B, the claim is that collective action causes change. Evidence: labor movements and online campaigns.” 因此社会运动解释使用的证据是劳工运动和在线运动。
questions.evidence: For column B, the claim is that collective action causes change. Evidence: labor movements and online campaigns

questions.prompt: True, False, or Not Given: Leo thinks the two explanations are completely separate.
questions.explanation: Leo说“So the two explanations are not completely separate.” 因此“Leo认为两种解释完全分离”是错误的。
questions.evidence: Leo: Exactly. So the two explanations are not completely separate.

questions.prompt: True, False, or Not Given: The teacher told the students to copy sentences from the articles.
questions.explanation: Mia说“The teacher said paraphrasing is important.” 意思是老师强调转述重要，而不是让抄写句子。因此“老师让学生抄写句子”是错误的。
questions.evidence: Mia: Yes. And we must use our own words, not copy sentences. The teacher said paraphrasing is important.

I think a better explanation combines them.
The first article argues that new tools create new behaviors.

For column B, the claim is that collective action causes change.
Evidence: labor movements and online campaigns.
The teacher said paraphrasing is important.

grammar.title: 名词性从句入门：that从句与情态动词条件表达
grammar.explanation: 英语中，that从句可以放在动词后作宾语，说明想法、事实或观点。例如：I think that technology is important. 这里的that可以省略，但书面语中常保留。注意：that从句本身有完整的主语和谓语。情态动词（can, could, may, might, must, should）与条件表达结合时，表示在某种条件下可能、必须或应该发生的事。例如：If we use technology, it can change our behavior. 条件句用if引导，主句用情态动词。今天重点：用that从句表达观点，用情态动词+条件句讨论可能性。
grammar.example: I think that technology is important, but it can't explain everything.

questions.evidence: Leo: Got it. Let's start writing the introduction now. We can say that social change is complex and different theories highlight different causes.

questions.explanation: that从句作believes的宾语，从句内部是完整句子“people choose how to use technology”。选项A正确。

questions.evidence: Mia: Right. The second one gives the example of remote work. It became common not just because of laptops, but because workers demanded flexibility.

materials.passage:
A city health team wants more people to walk to work. Last year, the team tested three campaign ideas with three different groups. The results are in the table below.

Table: Campaign test results (simulated data)

| Group | Main message | People who saw the message | People who walked more |
|-------|--------------|----------------------------|------------------------|
| A: Office workers | 'Walk 20 minutes a day' | 1,000 | 250 |
| B: Parents | 'Walk your children to school' | 800 | 320 |
| C: Older adults | 'Walk with a friend' | 600 | 210 |

Group B had the highest proportion of people who walked more. In Group B, 40% of people walked more. In Group A, the figure was 25%. So the proportion in Group B was 1.6 times as high as the proportion in Group A. Group C's proportion was 35%, which was higher than Group A's but lower than Group B's.

The team also looked at the number of people who walked more. Group A had 250 people, Group B had 320, and Group C had 210. Group B had the largest number, but the difference between Group A and Group B was only 70 people. The team noted that Group A's message reached more people (1,000) than Group B's message (800), but fewer people in Group A changed their behaviour. This shows that reaching a large audience does not always lead to more behaviour change. The message itself and how well it fits the audience may matter more. For example, parents may find it easy to walk their children to school because it fits their daily routine, while office workers may need a different reason to walk.

This year, the team is running a new campaign. They are using the message 'Walk with a friend' for all three groups. They believe this message will work well because it was the most effective message for older adults last year. However, they are not sure if it will work for office workers. The team is now collecting new data. They will compare this year's proportions with last year's proportions. They expect the proportion of office workers who walk more to rise from 25% to about 30%. They also expect the number of parents who walk more to stay about the same.

The team says that a message can work well for one group but not for another. They advise campaign planners to test messages with different audiences before using them city-wide. Testing helps planners see which messages work best for each audience. This can save time and money and make campaigns more effective. It also helps avoid wasting resources on messages that do not connect with a particular group.

materials.title: City Health Campaign: Choosing the Right Audience
materials.instructions: 本材料为原创模拟练习，不是官方雅思考试，也不代表任何分数。先听/读对话，注意倍数与比例表达、比较结构、过去和现在数据的时态选择。完成10道听力题后，学习语法讲解并做8道语法题，最后进行口语和写作迁移练习。所有答案依据原文，NOT GIVEN题需说明缺失信息。
materials.transcript:
Maya: Hi, Daniel. Thanks for coming. We need to plan the new city health campaign. The council wants to reach more people this year.
Daniel: Sure. What do we know about last year's campaign?
Maya: Last year we focused on young adults. We reached about 2,000 people. This year we have a bigger budget, so we can reach three times as many people.
Daniel: Three times as many? So 6,000 people?
Maya: Yes, 6,000. But the budget is only twice as big as last year's. So we must be careful.
Daniel: Right. Who should we target? Young adults again?
Maya: The data shows young adults are still important. But older people are now a larger group. Last year, people over 60 were 15 percent of the audience. This year, they are 25 percent.
Daniel: That's a big change. So we should include older people.
Maya: Exactly. But we also need to think about families. Families with children are 30 percent of the city population now. Last year, they were 20 percent.
Daniel: So families are one and a half times more common than before?
Maya: Yes, that's right. One and a half times. So we need materials for families too.
Daniel: What about the budget for each group? Last year we spent 50 percent on young adults. This year, we plan to spend 40 percent on young adults, 30 percent on older people, and 30 percent on families.
Maya: Good. But wait, last year we spent 50 percent on young adults and 50 percent on other groups. This year the total is 100 percent, but the groups are different.
Daniel: Yes. The young adult share is smaller, but the total budget is larger. So the money for young adults is still more than last year.
Maya: Let's check. Last year's budget was $10,000. This year it is $20,000. So 40 percent of $20,000 is $8,000. Last year, 50 percent of $10,000 was $5,000. So we are spending more on young adults, even though the percentage is lower.
Daniel: That's interesting. The percentage went down, but the amount went up.
Maya: Exactly. We need to explain that clearly in the report.
Daniel: What about the number of events? Last year we had 10 events. This year we plan to have 15 events. That's one and a half times as many.
Maya: Yes. And we want more people at each event. Last year, about 200 people came to each event. This year, we hope for 300 people at each event.
Daniel: So 15 events times 300 people is 4,500 people. But we said 6,000 people total.
Maya: Right. The 6,000 includes online reach. Online reach was 1,000 last year. This year we hope for 1,500 online.
Daniel: So 4,500 at events plus 1,500 online is 6,000. That works.
Maya: Good. Now, who will write the report?
Daniel: I can write it. But I need the exact numbers.
Maya: I'll send them today. And remember, the campaign starts next month.
Daniel: Got it. I'll start the draft tomorrow.

materials.title: The Bus Lane Puzzle: Correlation or Cause?
materials.instructions: 阅读一篇关于城市交通研究的模拟材料（所有数据均为虚构，仅用于教学）。先通读文章，理解研究小组如何区分相关与因果。然后完成10道阅读题（单选、填空、匹配、判断）。最后学习语法“倍数与比例表达；比较结构；过去和现在数据的时态选择”，并完成8道语法题。注意：填空题答案必须与原文完全一致，且不超过字数限制。
materials.passage:
A research group at a city university wanted to understand why traffic on Maple Avenue had become slower over a period of five years. The team, led by Dr. Chen, collected data from 2018 and 2023. They measured average travel time, bus passenger numbers, and the number of cars on the road. The results were surprising and challenged what many people believed.

In 2018, the average car trip along Maple Avenue took 18 minutes. By 2023, the same trip took 27 minutes. That is one and a half times longer than before. During the same period, the number of cars on the road rose from 12,000 per day to 18,000 per day. At the same time, the city added a bus lane in 2021. Some people said the bus lane caused the delay. They argued that fewer car lanes meant more congestion, so cars had to move more slowly.

Dr. Chen's team looked more carefully at the situation. They found that the bus lane actually carried more people than a car lane. A bus lane moved about 3,000 passengers per hour, while a car lane moved only 1,200 people per hour. This means the bus lane was two and a half times more efficient at moving people. However, the team also noticed that the number of cars had increased by 50% since 2018. This rise happened before the bus lane was built, so the bus lane could not be the reason for the earlier growth in traffic. The team concluded that the bus lane was not the main cause of slower traffic. The real cause was the growing number of cars.

To test this idea, the researchers compared Maple Avenue with Oak Street, which had no bus lane. Oak Street also saw a 50% increase in cars, and its travel time rose from 15 to 22 minutes. This was similar to what happened on Maple Avenue. The team said, "Correlation is not causation. Just because two things happen together does not mean one causes the other." In other words, two events can happen at the same time without one being the reason for the other.

The city now plans to add more bus lanes and also to improve traffic lights. Dr. Chen advises: "We need to look at the data carefully. A bus lane can be good for the city even if cars are slower." This shows that a measure like a bus lane can help many people travel efficiently, even when car drivers experience longer trips.

materials.title: City Traffic and Charts: Separating Correlation from Cause
materials.instructions: 本材料为原创模拟练习，非官方雅思试题，也不对应任何官方分数。请先听/读对话，注意研究小组如何区分相关与因果，以及倍数、比例和比较结构的使用。然后完成10道题（听力+阅读混合），再学习语法规则并完成8道语法题，最后进行口语和写作迁移练习。所有题目答案均来自原文，填空答案必须与原文完全一致。
materials.transcript:
Mia: So, team, thanks for coming. Let's look at the new city traffic data. Our question is simple: does the new bike lane on King Street reduce car use?

Leo: I pulled the numbers this morning. Car trips on King Street dropped by 18 percent after the lane opened. That's a big change.

Mia: It is. But wait — car trips on Queen Street also dropped by 15 percent, and there's no bike lane there. So something else may be happening.

Leo: Good point. Maybe more people are working from home this year. The city survey says remote work rose from 12 percent to 27 percent in the same period.

Mia: Exactly. So the bike lane and the drop in car trips are correlated, but we can't say the lane caused the drop. Correlation is not causation.

Leo: Right. To test cause, we need a comparison group. Queen Street can be our comparison group because it has no bike lane.

Mia: Perfect. Now, what about bus use? On King Street, bus trips were 2.5 times higher than before the lane. On Queen Street, bus trips were only 1.2 times higher.

Leo: So the increase on King Street is more than twice the increase on Queen Street. That's interesting.

Mia: Yes. But we still need to check other factors. For example, the city added two new bus routes on King Street last year. That could explain the bus increase.

Leo: True. So for buses, the new routes might be the cause, not the bike lane.

Mia: Let's write this down. We have three possible causes: the bike lane, remote work, and new bus routes. We need to separate them.

Leo: How about a simple chart? We can show car trips before and after on both streets. King Street: 10,000 car trips per day before, 8,200 after. Queen Street: 9,000 before, 7,650 after.

Mia: Good. So King Street dropped by 1,800 trips, and Queen Street dropped by 1,350 trips. The King Street drop is bigger, but not huge.

Leo: And the percentage drop is 18 percent on King Street and 15 percent on Queen Street. So the difference is only 3 percentage points.

Mia: That's small. It suggests the bike lane may not be the main cause. Remote work is probably a bigger factor.

Leo: Should we say the bike lane had no effect?

Mia: No, we can't say that either. We just don't have enough evidence. We need a controlled study. For now, we can say the data shows a correlation, not a cause.

Leo: Got it. So our report will say: car trips fell on both streets, but the fall was similar. The bike lane is one possible factor, but remote work and new bus routes are also important.

Mia: Exactly. And we should use careful language: 'may be associated with' instead of 'caused by'.

Leo: Agreed. I'll make the chart with before and after numbers for both streets.

Mia: Great. Let's meet again on Friday to review the draft.

materials.title: New Bus Lanes in Riverside: Who Wins and Who Loses?
materials.instructions: 这是为B1–B2成人学习者设计的原创模拟阅读材料（非官方雅思，也不对应任何官方分数）。先通读文章，再完成10道题。题目全部为英文，解释为中文。注意：本材料重点复习被动语态、顺序连接词，并新学“定语从句与分词短语的辨认”。请先看语法讲解，再做题。
materials.passage:
A. Riverside is a mid-sized city with a busy river, three bridges, and a lot of old roads. Last year, the city council introduced a new transport policy. Two main roads in the city centre were changed. One lane on each road was closed to private cars and opened only to buses and bicycles. The plan was called 'Clean Lanes'. The council said the plan was designed to reduce traffic and air pollution. Many people supported the idea, but not everyone was happy.

B. The new rules were introduced in March. First, the council held three public meetings. Then, engineers studied traffic on the two roads for six weeks. After that, the changes were tested for two months. Finally, the policy was made permanent in September. During the test, bus travel times fell by about 15 percent. Air quality near the roads also improved. However, drivers who used the roads every day were angry. They said the new lanes made their journeys longer. Some shop owners on Bridge Street also complained. They said fewer customers came by car, so they lost money.

C. The council listened to these complaints. In October, it published a report written by a team of transport experts. The report showed that bus passengers and cyclists benefited most. People living near the roads also benefited, because the air was cleaner. But drivers and some local businesses lost out. The report suggested two solutions. The first was to build new parking areas near the edge of the city centre. The second was to give small shops a reduction in their business taxes. The council is now discussing these ideas.

D. Not everyone agrees with the report. A group of drivers, called 'Fair Roads', says the policy is unfair. They argue that people who live outside the city and drive to work have no good bus service. They also say that the council did not ask them before making the changes. The council replies that the public meetings were open to everyone. It also says that new bus routes to the outer areas will start next year. Meanwhile, some environmental groups want the city to go further. They want more Clean Lanes and fewer cars in the centre.

E. The story of Riverside is not unusual. Many cities are trying to reduce cars in their centres. The effects of such policies are often unequal. People who take the bus or ride a bike usually gain. People who must drive often lose. The challenge for city leaders is to listen to all groups and to find fair solutions. As one council member said, 'A good transport policy must work for everyone, not just for some.'

grammar.title: 被动语态、顺序连接词、定语从句与分词短语的辨认
grammar.explanation: 本课复习被动语态（be + 过去分词，强调动作承受者）和顺序连接词（first, then, after that, finally）。新学内容是辨认定语从句和分词短语：定语从句用who/which/that等引导，放在名词后补充说明；分词短语用-ing或-ed形式放在名词后，起类似作用，但更简短。例如：a report written by experts（分词短语）相当于a report which was written by experts（定语从句）。
grammar.example: In October, it published a report written by a team of transport experts.

materials.transcript:
Maya: Hi, Tom. Did you see the new bus lane on King Street? It opened last Monday.
Tom: Yes, I did. But I'm not sure it's fair. The lane was built very quickly, and now the shops on that street are losing customers.
Maya: Really? I thought the bus lane would help everyone. Buses are faster now, right?
Tom: They are, but only for people who take the bus. The problem is that the lane was placed on the busiest shopping street. First, the council removed all the parking spaces. Then, they painted the lane red. After that, they banned cars from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m.
Maya: So shop owners are angry because their customers can't park?
Tom: Exactly. The shop owners who were interviewed by the local newspaper said their sales dropped by 30 percent. One owner, Mrs. Chen, who runs a bakery, said she might close her shop.
Maya: That's terrible. But the bus passengers are happy, aren't they?
Tom: Many are. The bus ride from the station to the market, which used to take 25 minutes, now takes only 12 minutes. People who live far from the city center save a lot of time.
Maya: So the policy helps some people and hurts others. Is the council doing anything about it?
Tom: They are reviewing the plan. A meeting was held last night, and the council promised to listen to shop owners. But no decision has been made yet.
Maya: I see. Maybe they could add some parking spaces on a side street.
Tom: That's a good idea. The council said they would consider it. But for now, the bus lane stays.

grammar.title: 被动语态、顺序连接词、定语从句与分词短语的辨认
grammar.explanation: 本课重点：1) 被动语态：be + 过去分词，强调动作承受者，如“The lane was built.”。2) 顺序连接词：first, then, after that, finally，表示步骤顺序。3) 定语从句：who/which/that 引导，修饰名词，如“the shop owners who were interviewed”。4) 分词短语：现在分词(-ing)或过去分词(-ed)短语作定语或状语，如“People living far from the city center”或“Interviewed by the newspaper, the owners...”。注意区分被动语态与过去分词短语作定语。

materials.title: The Riverside Community Panel: Weighing Costs and Public Benefits
materials.instructions: 这是一份为B1–B2成人学习者设计的原创模拟阅读材料（非官方雅思测试，也不对应任何官方分数）。请先通读文章，理解一个社区小组如何比较项目成本与公共收益。然后完成10道阅读题（单选、填空、匹配、判断正误/未提及）。最后学习语法部分：本课新讲“被动语态”，并复习“顺序连接词”和“定语从句与分词短语的辨认”。所有题目和选项均为英文，解释为中文。填空答案必须与原文完全一致，并注意字数限制。
materials.passage:
A. In the small town of Riverton, a community group called the Riverside Panel was formed last year. The panel was asked to compare three possible projects for the old riverside area. The town council wanted a clear report before any money was spent. The panel’s job was not to choose a favourite project but to show the costs and the public benefits of each one. The members met twice a month in the library, and their discussions were recorded by a volunteer. The final report was published in June and was sent to every household in Riverton.

B. The first project, called the River Walk, would create a path for walking and cycling along the river. The path would be built by a local company, and the work would take about eight months. The cost was estimated at 1.2 million dollars. The panel noted that the River Walk would be used by families, runners, and older people who want a safe place to exercise. The benefits were described as “daily and free.” However, some members worried that the path might be damaged by floods in winter. The panel agreed that this risk should be studied further before construction begins.

C. The second project was a small outdoor market near the bridge. The market would be opened on Saturdays and would be run by local farmers and craftspeople. The start-up cost was much lower, at 300,000 dollars. The panel found that the market would support about forty small businesses and would bring visitors into the town centre. The benefits would be economic and social: farmers would sell directly to customers, and neighbours would meet each other more often. The main problem was parking. The panel reported that the area around the bridge is already crowded on weekends, and new parking spaces would be needed. That extra cost was not included in the first estimate.

D. The third project was a new community centre with a sports hall and a meeting room. The building would be designed by an architect from the city, and it would be paid for partly by the council and partly by a private donor. The total cost was 2.5 million dollars, the highest of the three. The panel said that the centre would be used all year, in all weather, and that it would offer classes for children and adults. The benefits were clear but the costs were high, and the panel warned that running costs, such as heating and staff, would continue for many years. The donor’s money would cover only the building, not the daily costs.

E. After comparing the three projects, the panel wrote a short conclusion. It said that the River Walk had the lowest cost per user and the most daily benefits, but it also had the flood risk. The market had the lowest start-up cost and strong economic benefits, but it needed parking. The community centre had the widest range of benefits, but it was the most expensive to build and to run. The panel did not recommend one project. Instead, it suggested that the council should first pay for a flood study and a parking survey, and then decide. The report ended with a simple sentence: “Good decisions are made when costs and benefits are seen together.”

To compare the costs and public benefits of three projects
To build a new path along the river
To collect money from local families
answers: To compare the costs and public benefits of three projects
questions.explanation: 原文A段明确说“The panel was asked to compare three possible projects”，并且“to show the costs and the public benefits of each one”。因此选第二项。
questions.evidence: The panel was asked to compare three possible projects for the old riverside area.

grammar.explanation: 本课新讲“被动语态”。当我们更关心“事情被做”而不是“谁做”时，用 be + 过去分词。例如原文“The path would be built by a local company.” 这里重点是路径会被建造，建造者用 by 引出。复习部分：顺序连接词（first, then, after, finally）帮助排列步骤；定语从句用 who/which/that 补充说明名词；分词短语用 -ing 或 -ed 开头，省略主语和 be 动词，例如“called the River Walk”等于“which is called the River Walk”。注意：被动语态是本课新规则，顺序连接词和分词短语是复习内容。

materials.title: Panel Review: Comparing Costs and Public Benefits of a Community Garden Proposal
materials.instructions: 本材料为模拟英语学习材料，非官方雅思考试。请先听录音（或阅读文字稿），然后完成10道听力/阅读题。题目类型包括单选、填空、匹配（以单选形式）和判断正误/未提及。填空题答案必须来自原文，且不超过字数限制。语法部分先学习新规则（被动语态、顺序连接词、定语从句与分词短语的辨认），再完成8道独立新句子的语法题。最后进行口语和写作迁移练习。
materials.transcript:
Host: Welcome to today's panel. We are comparing the costs and public benefits of a community garden proposal for the old railway land. Let me introduce our panel: Maria, a city planner; Tom, a local business owner; and Dr. Chen, an environmental economist. Maria, can you start?
Maria: Thank you. The proposal was written by the neighborhood association last year. The land, which has been unused for a decade, would be divided into 40 small plots. Each plot would be rented to a family for a small fee. The garden would be managed by a volunteer committee. First, the soil must be tested for safety. After that, water pipes will be installed. Then, the plots will be given to families. Finally, a small tool shed will be built.
Tom: I have concerns. The initial cost, which is estimated at $50,000, would be paid by the city. That money could be used for other projects. Also, parking spaces would be lost. Some of my customers already complain about parking.
Dr. Chen: Those are valid points. However, the long-term benefits should also be considered. Studies show that community gardens can reduce stress and improve mental health. The garden would provide fresh vegetables for about 60 families. Moreover, the green space would absorb rainwater, which helps prevent flooding. The benefits, when compared to the costs, are likely to be higher over ten years.
Host: Tom, what would you suggest?
Tom: I suggest a smaller garden, perhaps 20 plots, and keeping some parking. That way, costs would be reduced and parking would still be available.
Maria: That is a reasonable compromise. The committee could start with 20 plots and expand later if the garden is successful. The soil test, which is required by law, would still be done first.
Host: Thank you all. So, the key points are: the garden would be built on unused land, costs would be shared, and benefits would include fresh food and flood prevention. We will now take questions from the audience.

materials.title: The Attention Study: How Visitors and Locals Share a Museum
materials.instructions: 阅读下面的文章，完成10个问题。文章和题目均为原创模拟材料，不是雅思真题，也不代表任何官方分数。先读文章，再做题；填空题答案必须与原文完全一致，且不超过字数限制。语法部分先看中文讲解，再完成8道新句子的练习。
materials.passage:
A
Last spring, a small city museum invited two researchers to study how visitors allocate attention. The museum, which had recently redesigned three of its galleries, wanted to know whether people actually looked at the objects or simply walked past them. The researchers, Dr. Lena Ortiz and Dr. Samir Haddad, installed small cameras above each doorway. Although the cameras recorded only movement, not faces, some visitors felt uneasy. Nevertheless, the museum kept the study running because the data promised to improve the visitor experience.

B
The first gallery, called 'Everyday Objects', contained ordinary things: a worn wooden spoon, a child's shoe, and a cracked teapot. Surprisingly, visitors spent more time in front of the spoon than in front of the teapot. Ortiz believes that the spoon's label, which told a short story about a grandmother's kitchen, encouraged people to stop. In contrast, the teapot's label gave only a date and a place. 'When a label offers a story,' Ortiz explained, 'visitors treat the object as a character rather than an artifact.'

C
The second gallery displayed large paintings. Here, the pattern reversed. Visitors moved quickly past the paintings, even though the paintings were famous. Haddad noticed that people often glanced at a painting, checked their phones, and then moved on. He suggests that large artworks can feel overwhelming, whereas small objects invite close looking. The third gallery, which focused on local history, produced the most surprising result. Local residents, who had visited the museum as children, spent almost twice as long in this gallery as tourists did. They paused at photographs of streets they remembered and pointed out buildings to their families.

D
However, not everyone behaved as expected. A few tourists lingered in the local history gallery for over an hour, reading every label. Some residents, on the other hand, walked through it in less than five minutes. 'Attention is personal,' Haddad said. 'A familiar object can be boring to one person and fascinating to another.' The researchers concluded that museums should offer different kinds of labels: some with stories, some with facts, and some with questions. In this way, every visitor, whether local or foreign, might find something worth a second look.

E
The study also revealed a practical problem. The cameras sometimes failed to record when the galleries were crowded. As a result, the researchers lost data from busy weekends. Despite this limitation, the museum decided to use the findings. Next year, it will add story labels to twenty more objects. The director, who initially doubted the project, now calls it 'the most useful study we have ever done'. Whether other museums will follow this example remains to be seen.

grammar.explanation: 本课重点有三类结构。第一，让步与对比：although/even though/though 表示“虽然”，后面接完整句子；whereas/while 表示“而”，用于对比两个分句；despite/in spite of 后面接名词或动名词，不接句子。第二，关系从句：who 指人，which 指物，that 可指人或物；非限制性关系从句用逗号隔开，补充信息。第三，举例表达：for example, for instance, such as, like, including 都可以举例，但 such as 和 including 后面通常接名词或名词短语，不接完整句子。注意：新学形式是“despite + 名词/动名词”和“非限制性关系从句”；复习形式是“although + 句子”和“such as + 名词”。

materials.instructions: 这是一份为B2–C1成人学习者设计的英语听力与语法练习，主题为旅游与文化讨论。请先听/读对话，再完成10道听力题（含单选、填空、判断正误/未提及）。然后学习语法讲解并完成8道语法题。所有题目答案均来自原文，请勿凭常识作答。本材料为模拟教学材料，非官方雅思试题。
materials.transcript:
Mia: Hi, everyone. Thanks for coming to the museum today. I'm Mia, the study coordinator. This is a short study about how visitors allocate attention. Before we start, can I ask you a few questions?

Ben: Sure. I'm Ben. I usually spend a lot of time reading the labels, but my friend Leo just walks quickly and looks at the big paintings.

Mia: That's interesting. So, Ben, you focus on details, while Leo prefers a fast overview. Leo, is that right?

Leo: Yes, mostly. Although I sometimes stop for a sculpture, I don't read much. I take a photo and move on.

Mia: OK. Now, please wear this small eye-tracking glasses. They record where you look. The glasses are light, but they may feel strange at first.

Ben: Do they hurt? 

Mia: No, they don't. They just sit on your head. Please don't touch them during the visit.

Leo: How long is the visit?

Mia: About forty minutes. You can walk anywhere, but please stay in the main galleries. The special exhibition is closed today.

Ben: What are we looking for?

Mia: We want to know which parts of a painting people look at first. Some people look at faces, and others look at colors or shapes. There is no right answer.

Leo: So, we just look naturally?

Mia: Exactly. After the visit, I'll ask you to draw a quick map of one painting from memory. That will show what you noticed.

Ben: I'm not good at drawing.

Mia: Don't worry. It's not a test of art. It's just a memory task. Oh, and one more thing: please don't discuss the paintings with each other during the visit. You can talk afterwards.

Leo: Can we use our phones?

Mia: You can take photos, but please don't use social media inside the galleries. The light from screens can affect the eye-tracking data.

Ben: Got it. So, we look, we don't talk, and we don't post.

Mia: That's right. Any other questions? No? Great. Let's begin. Remember, the study is about attention, not about knowledge. Just be yourselves.
